In IIA large volume, use the intersection matrix K_ij=K_ijk e₀ᵏ and its kernel to identify rigid fields; the stated rank is r_rigid=nV−rank(K)−λ, with λ=0 for decompactification and 1 for emergent strings.

Use a homogeneous degree-two prepotential, symplectic periods, and special Kähler identities to relate scalar metrics, gauge kinetic matrices, central charges, and charge-to-mass ratios. The scalar-curvature expression has a negative constant −2nV(nV+1) plus a nonnegative Yukawa-coupling contraction, locating the possible divergent contribution.

Modify CLASS to compute CMB angular spectra, matter power spectra, and late-time growth. Representative ζ scans compare pure exponential potentials with potentials having a local minimum, after calibrating present-day energy densities.

Average rapid axion oscillations using the Madelung formulation. The effective mass is m(t)=m_a/W(χ̄), and the homogeneous physical axion density evolves as ρ̄_ax=Cm(t)/a³, yielding an interacting nonrelativistic fluid.
Develop homogeneous, spatially flat FLRW evolution and linear scalar perturbations in conformal-Newtonian gauge, assuming no anisotropic stress. The numerical implementation uses synchronous gauge.

Add total derivatives before eliminating auxiliary current blocks, thereby exposing Wess–Zumino terms. For the membrane branch, substitute the field-dependent world-volume projection ∂ᵐ=εⁱʲ(∂ⱼxᵐ)∂ᵢ and choose the membrane world-volume metric to obtain the determinant action.

Construct brane current algebras with invariant-tensor Schwinger terms and impose Virasoro and Gauss-law constraints. Replacing momenta by zero-mode derivatives gives dimensional-reduction and section conditions: Virasoro sectioning reduces spacetime, while Gauss-law sectioning reduces the world-volume.

Use the double-zweibein Hamiltonian and Legendre transformation to obtain a doubled string Lagrangian bilinear in selfdual and anti-selfdual currents. Gauge choices remove the extra current-square multipliers; vielbeins convert the currents to local flat indices for reduction.

Use a thermal scalar spectrum and the standard cold-inflation tensor spectrum, adopting the imported fit G(Q)≈1+0.18Q^1.4+0.01Q^1.8. The paper also imposes its stated COBE normalization U/ε≈(0.0276Mp)^4 to constrain couplings.

Following prior work, add thermal radiation entropy inside a Hubble volume to the Bousso/Gibbons–Hawking entropy comparison, then differentiate the resulting bound to estimate a correction to the swampland slope coefficient.
Transform to the Einstein frame, express canonical-field slow-roll quantities through the radial field ϕ, and approximate the Q-weighted e-fold integral in the large-field, strong-dissipation limit.

Integrate over instanton size with a dρ/ρ5 measure, include the classical instanton weight and collective-coordinate factors, and close all fermion legs using available interactions. Split the size integral at the heavy axion-sector threshold λfa.

Mass insertions replace fermion bilinears by mψρ, whereas Yukawa closures introduce yψ without additional powers of ρ. Normalized zero-mode wavefunctions are used to estimate a 1/π2 suppression per loop, up to order-one factors.

Construct gravitational analogues of ’t Hooft vertices by solving the normalizable, massless Dirac equation twisted by the background gauge connection. Appendix B explicitly counts zero modes and notes the Atiyah–Patodi–Singer index theorem as an alternative.

Compare horizon existence and photon-sphere charges in selected M > Q, M = Q, and Q > M configurations. Vary a, c, and ω at fixed ℓ = 1; numerical examples and a summary table supply the reported compatibility classifications.

Introduce the photon-sphere potential H(r,θ) = sqrt(f(r)/h(r))/sinθ and identify candidate photon-sphere radii through ∂rH = 0. A two-component vector field is formed from radially and angularly weighted derivatives of H.

Assign local winding numbers around zeros of the vector field and sum them to obtain the photon-sphere topological charge. The text allows individual charges ±1 and total charges −1, 0, or +1 for the chosen contours.

The stability discussion uses characteristic initial data, linear wave and gravitational perturbations, horizon conservation laws, and semilinear model equations to investigate which nonlinear structures might permit stability despite horizon instabilities.

Unruh reviews field quantization using affine versus Killing horizon parameters, observer-dependent particle detection, and analogue-gravity calculations and experiments. These support robustness arguments but leave a requested derivation avoiding super-Planckian modes outstanding.

Berti reviews parametrized post-Einsteinian inspiral tests and three modified-gravity QNM approaches: metric perturbations at low spin, potentially large coupling; generalized Teukolsky equations at small coupling; and spectral methods allowing arbitrary coupling, with practical rotation limits.

For photon spheres, use H(r,θ) = sqrt(f(r)/h(r))/sinθ, solve ∂rH = 0, construct a weighted gradient vector, and sum winding numbers around its zeros. Numerical examples compare these charges with the paper’s extremal Q/M criterion.

Apply Duan’s ϕ-mapping framework to the generalized off-shell free energy F = M − S/τ. The thermodynamic vector is (∂F/∂rH, −cotΘ cscΘ); zeros carry winding numbers whose sum W defines the reported thermodynamic class.

Determine candidate extremal configurations by separating the horizon equation into Reissner–Nordström and fluid functions fL and fR, then imposing equality of both functions and their slopes at r0. The authors use this tangency construction to obtain r0, αext, and an extremal charge-to-mass relation.

Linearized Fourier equations separate longitudinal and transverse polarizations; WKB evolution and Mathieu-equation growth estimates describe changing masses and resonant production. Clockwork backreaction is analyzed by perturbing its gauge-field mass matrix.
One-loop scalar effective potentials are computed with a finite UV cutoff and the additional path-integral determinant required by noncanonical kinetic terms.

For finite real coupling, KK-dependent complex integration rays are grouped separately in the upper and lower half-planes. Convergent geometric KK sums combine into a closed contour; residues distinguish ordinary GV contributions, exponential corrections, and coincident poles.

The supersymmetric particle worldline supplies the d4θ measure through universal fermionic zero modes. For a rigid genus-r cycle, additional zero modes enter a helicity supertrace and change the sine denominator power from 2 to 2−2r.

A Gaussian charged-scalar integral becomes a functional determinant, then a Schwinger proper-time heat-kernel trace. The anti-self-dual background factorizes the trace into two planar Landau-level systems, including their spatial degeneracy.

Counts states on the proposed S²×R² surface phase space using dz/dp=Ap/ℏ² and nonrelativistic momentum–energy relations. Integrating yields the proposed asymmetry energy E=ℏ²c⁴z²/(32πG²M²m_g), used in a Boltzmann-type characteristic function.

Defines instability through ∂ρ/∂(1/M²)<0. For cutoffs, integrates the state density, identifies a logarithmic radial divergence, and introduces interval estimation with a gamma family of shape α=2 and parameter β=z, using incomplete-gamma probabilities.

The sequestered-model modulino mass is evaluated from a one-loop gravitational KK sum with the unbroken-SUSY contribution subtracted. The result uses a polylogarithmic function f(ω) and scales as m̃z=f(ω)/[(4π)²Mp²R³].

Experimental reach is taken from previously derived projected contours, using the Feldman–Cousins procedure: FASERν with 150 fb−1 and FLArE with 3 ab−1, with 68% and 95% confidence contours. These are sensitivity forecasts.
Oscillation phenomenology uses H=UM²U†/(2E), a unitary four-state mixing matrix, and the short-baseline limit. The resulting survival probability is Pαα=1−4|Uα4|²(1−|Uα4|²)sin²(Δm²41 L/(4E)).

Explicit tools include Kähler-coordinate changes, scalar-potential Hessians with kinetic normalization, matching radius kinetic terms to toroidal dimensional reduction, and relating slow-roll e-fold integrals to KK species counts.

The paper reviews scalar-tensor equivalence using an auxiliary scalar, a Lagrange multiplier, Gaussian elimination, and a Weyl transformation. Allowing field-dependent curvature coupling and transforming between string and Einstein frames incorporates the dilaton; the geometric rewriting also contains dilaton-derivative terms.

Reformulate Friedmann and scalar equations in H0t or N=ln a, using their differential dependence to solve a sufficient subset. Numerical solutions illustrate the analytic approximations; a dynamical-system formulation is also used for the exponential example.

Solve successive two-component backgrounds; invert the radiation–matter t(a) relation by Cardan–Tartaglia with continuous branch selection. Treat scalar evolution on that background using local power laws and approximately constant potential derivatives; use continuity-equation integrals for the latest phase.

Construct independent local coupling bases using Bianchi identities and integration by parts; circle-reduce them and impose restricted Buscher invariance modulo base-space total derivatives. Tree-level equations of motion are then used to identify removable multiplets.

Test type-II covariance by allowing different IIA/IIB coefficients and requiring the reduced IIA action to map to IIB. Separately allow genus corrections to heterotic transformations, which generate additional one-loop contributions through variation of the tree-level action.

Estimates the one-loop prefactor by dimensional scaling rather than evaluating its determinant. Removing D translational zero modes gives the determinant ratio mass dimension −2D; the authors write A∼(B/2π)^(D/2) a m_-^D, with an undetermined dimensionless factor a.

Uses the Callan–Coleman–de Luccia semiclassical rate Γ/V_(D−1)=A exp(−B/ℏ), with B the bounce action minus the false-vacuum action. The thin-wall treatment separates interior, wall and exterior contributions; fluctuation operators are decomposed into spherical harmonics and KK modes.

Construct the generalized Lie derivative using the adjoint projector in End(56); impose Y^{MN}_{PQ} ∂M⊗∂N=0. Highest-GL(1)-weight coordinates in GL(6)×SL(2) and GL(7) branchings provide the IIB and eleven-dimensional sections.

Toroidal KK reduction, flat-index field redefinitions producing improved field strengths, and electromagnetic dualization through Bianchi identities or Lagrange multipliers expose lower-dimensional symmetry structures.

The generalized Scherk–Schwarz ansatz factors internal dependence through an exceptional-group-valued twist U(Y) and scale factor ρ(Y). Differential consistency equations identify the lower-dimensional embedding tensor.

Metric implementations pair the global-potential ansatz ω̃=ωref+i∂∂̄φ with a Monge–Ampère loss, and a positive global-section update to the ambient Fubini–Study metric with the squared metric norm of the Einstein tensor. Global neural-network functions parameterize the unknown coefficients; JAX supplies differentiation, vectorization, and compilation.

Reduce tensor PDEs to optimization over global scalar or vector-valued functions. Construct tensor sections from pulled-back ambient twisted forms, untwist with line-bundle sections, and take tensor products and appropriate symmetrizations; alternatively add exact corrections to reference cohomology representatives.

Harmonic TX-valued forms are modeled as Φ+∂̄V s using Kodaira–Spencer reference representatives and global sections s; cohomology is fixed by construction, so the loss enforces co-closure. Independent losses can be summed across moduli directions. Monte Carlo integration evaluates the Weil–Petersson metric, with a deformation-theoretic computation providing a separate route.

Write relative entropy in terms of Euclidean effective actions, integrate fields using tree-level saddle points, and expand in a bookkeeping parameter multiplying heavy–light interactions. General expressions are developed through cubic order; the two-field examples are evaluated through sixth order and compared with all-interaction-order tree-level results.

Match inflationary fluctuations through X³ onto sound-speed and cubic-interaction parameters, then relate entropy inequalities to fNL. The paper compares the resulting restrictions with displayed observational confidence regions and with imported five- and six-point scattering perturbative-unitarity bounds.

Translates higher-dimensional functionals using reduction rules, and computes Chern–Simons gauge variations on finite regions. Supergravity equations of motion turn the required form-field boundary terms into on-shell bulk expressions.
Uses the imported complexity=anything framework: optimize one functional to select a codimension-zero region, then evaluate another functional there. Hypersurface functionals arise as a special case.

Applies imported boundary Morse–Bott inequalities: Σ_j P_t(C_j)t^{λ_j}+P_t(C)−P_t(B)=(1+t)R(t), with R having nonnegative integer coefficients. Critical loci encode cycle degenerations; a shrinking cycle has dimension c+λ−1, and the final collapse satisfies c+λ−1=n.
Uses the integral homology long exact sequence of (B,C), Lefschetz duality and the Universal Coefficient Theorem to constrain bordism homology. Mayer–Vietoris is used when gluing two bubble bordisms.

Apply the Hardy–Littlewood Laplace-transform Tauberian theorem to positive energy moments of impact-parameter partial waves. Partial-wave asymptotics and absolute convergence permit passage to the impact-parameter representation.

Smear momentum transfer t=−q² with ψ_a(q)=(q/q₀)^a(1−q/q₀)^{(d−1)/2}, 0<a≤d−4. In suitable nonempty complex-energy regions, unitarity makes the UV dispersive integral nonnegative; a→0 converts the graviton pole into a 1/a singularity.

In AdS, combine impact-parameter blocks, a Mellin contour representation of the eikonal phase, hyperbolic spectral decomposition, and the Lorentzian inversion formula to extract operator poles and residues.

Uses the two-dimensional trace anomaly T^μ_μ = R/(24π), with R = −n″, and stress-tensor conservation. Integration constants are selected using the stated Unruh conditions: no ingoing flux at infinity and vanishing T_uu at the past horizon.

Integrates an inherited primordial-black-hole mass spectrum to estimate abundance. The appendix obtains effective matter density and pressures from the Einstein tensor of the regular four-dimensional metrics and evaluates energy-condition inequalities.

Relates temperature and radiation flux to surface gravity. Since an exact analytic horizon location and evaporation-time integral are unavailable, a second-order small-r expansion of n(r) is used to estimate a possible remnant as the horizon radius tends to zero.

Replace all compactification fluxes across a domain wall by zero, impose tadpole cancellation, and include the lower-dimensional branes required on the fluxless side. Their endpoints form spikes on the wall.

For AdS₃, zoom into coincident M5–M5′–M2 intersections, smear along the M2 direction, and take a near-brane decoupling limit. Flux integrals relate density parameters to quantized charges, allowing a holographic central-charge calculation.

For AdS₄, use a warped AdS₄×S²×S² geometry over a disc-like Riemann surface, controlled by two harmonic functions. Their pole separation fixes D3 charge and an internal-volume expression that the authors maximize.

Five-stage filtering enumerates zero/nonzero patterns, tests Bianchi identities, adds stationarity, imposes V=0 or V>0, then checks Hessian positivity. Mathematica Reduce performs compatibility tests; NSolve subsequently explores a reduced set.

Axionic flux orbits absorb axions into flux combinations. Four γ and ten λ quantities additionally absorb saxion powers, expressing the required constraints as real algebraic equalities and inequalities without explicitly solving the original moduli equations.

The stability test requires all six leading principal determinants of the real symmetric 6×6 Hessian to be strictly positive. The authors report that saxion dependence factors out of these determinants.

Performs preliminary CMB-distance calibration using D_M(z_star) = 13869.6 Mpc and physical matter density. Because radiation is omitted, replaces Ω_m0 h² = 0.14314 by 0.1444; tests against reference cases motivate an approximately 1% estimation accuracy. This is not a full CMB-spectrum likelihood analysis.

Because H(z) is implicit, uses H as a parameter, derives z(H), dH/dN, curvature and deceleration, and combines numerical exploration with implicit-function analysis. Effective density, pressure, and equation of state follow from the modified Friedmann equations.

Classifies parameter branches using Ω_m0 = (1 − 2β)e^β and its inversion through the two real Lambert-W branches. The theoretical exploration includes four regions and three special points, including regions with negative matter density that are not accepted as physical cosmologies.

Sharp o-minimality organizes definable sets into a chosen double filtration ΩF,D. Logical unions/intersections add degrees and maximize formats; complements and linear projections preserve filtration bounds. Fixed-format one-dimensional component counts are bounded by an explicitly computable polynomial PF(D).

Pfaffian functions are represented by a finite triangular differential chain: each derivative of ζi is polynomial in the variables and ζ1,…,ζi. The working assignment is F=n+r and D=deg P+Σij deg Pij.

Direct-scattering rates integrate differential cross sections over the laboratory velocity distribution, with density normalization ρχ/mχ. At momentum transfer well below GeV, quark/gluon interactions are matched onto nucleons and pions, then nuclei. Indirect annihilation calculations use J(Ω)=∫los ρχ² dx.

Organizes hidden-sector interactions by EFT operator dimension and low-dimension portals. Collider interpretations use explicit-mediator simplified models and matching to low-energy EFT; the contact-interaction description fails when collision energies approach or exceed mediator masses.

Reviews thermal relic estimates using thermally averaged annihilation cross sections and perturbative partial waves: the velocity factor scales as v^(2ℓ), with ℓ=0 for s-wave and ℓ=1 for p-wave annihilation.

A Wilsonian momentum-shell argument estimates typical scalar fluctuations and approximates scalar/gauge factorization at high cutoff. The authors then use the dilute instanton gas size integral and one-loop gauge running to estimate the contribution.

Weyl transformation and canonical normalization introduce F(φ) = h(φ)/Ω(φ). A two-loop Yukawa contribution to gluon wave-function renormalization requires a counterterm proportional to (∂φF)² tr(GG), including an arbitrary finite coefficient.

An illustrative lattice calculation samples free-field Fourier fluctuations to exhibit large, rapidly varying scalar configurations and a small fraction of low-field points. It supports the fluctuation picture rather than simulating the full interacting instanton problem.

Compute H1 of the proposed smooth quotient by abelianizing its fundamental group, and determine H2 using Poincaré duality. The reported groups are H0=H2=H3=Z and H1=Z⊕Z2⊕Z2; wrapped M-theory objects provide a geometric brane interpretation.

Construct torus, Klein bottle, annulus and Möbius amplitudes; transform between loop and transverse channels using modular S and P transformations. Extract Chan–Paton representations, RR couplings and tachyons to assess D-brane charges and stability.

Use Poisson summation, modular unfolding and oscillator expansions to compute vacuum energy. The large-radius expansion separates supergravity KK contributions from string oscillator terms expressed through modified Bessel functions.

Two UV models are analyzed: a GUP-deformed momentum-space action, inner product and shell matching; and an SFT-inspired nonlocal free-field model whose Wightman function determines detector observables and modified number expectations.

The chapter reviews S-matrix estimates for particle creation by Planck-suppressed higher-derivative curvature/radiation and matter/radiation interactions, tracking their exponential dependence on retarded detection time.

Localized, narrow-frequency wave packets and Bogoliubov transformations are used to calculate number expectations as functions of detection time. This distinguishes the thermal spectral factor from the time-dependent magnitude of radiation.

Introduce g_total=g+εh with a perturbation proportional to the cosmological constant; derive perturbed thermodynamic quantities and compare extremal-mass derivatives with entropy and pressure response identities.

Solve the T=0 charge–entropy relation numerically because an exact inversion is unavailable. For selected charges and fixed remaining parameters, evaluate extremal masses at different ε and compare the resulting curves with M=Q.

Separate the charged Klein–Gordon equation into spherical harmonics and a radial equation, use a tortoise coordinate and ingoing horizon modes to calculate fluxes, then Taylor-expand the metric function at its minimum to test horizon persistence.
Solve f(r+)=0 for the mass, express it through each generalized entropy, and present temperature, electric potential and thermodynamic volume together with a first law dM=T dS+Φ dQ+V dP.

Expand perturbed masses in ε, solve the mass relation for ε, and differentiate entropy at fixed modified mass and extensive variables. Compare the resulting temperature-weighted derivative with the mass-shift expression, then introduce an entropy Jacobian factor.

Estimate confinement using one-loop gauge running with heavy particles decoupled at mass thresholds. Match to chiral Lagrangians for light quarks and use naive dimensional analysis for heavy-quark regimes, choosing coefficients to interpolate continuously.

For universes without doublet or triplet VEVs, integrate out scalars to obtain dimension-six four-fermion operators, match Yukawa spurions to a six-flavor chiral Lagrangian, and integrate out neutral pions to extract the ALP potential.

Compute instanton-size integrals across successive SU(5), supersymmetric SM-group, and low-energy effective theories. Use anomalous axial and generalized R-symmetry spurion rules to constrain Yukawa determinants and SUSY-breaking factors; compare numerical integrals with asymptotic approximations.

Dimensionally reduce the near-horizon Einstein–Maxwell theory to JT gravity, integrate the dilaton to constrain curvature, and integrate Schwarzian boundary fluctuations exactly while treating other modes semiclassically.

Compute neutral emission with Schwarzian two-point functions and Fermi’s golden rule, coupling the throat to asymptotic radiation through greybody matching. Diphoton emission uses second-order perturbation theory, JT four-point functions, and angular momentum projections.

Construct charged worldline gravitational instantons with junction conditions; integrate almost-zero modes and resum winding and multiple-defect configurations. The moduli-space calculation uses a deformation of (2,p) minimal-string mathematics, without interpreting the corrections as stringy.

Separate lognormal-dip and tanh-suppression diagnostic primordial templates remove subsequent oscillations. Planck fitting and forecasts using their respective best-fit fiducials isolate large-scale detectability from correlated short-scale effects.

Fits use Planck lowT/lowE likelihoods at ℓ=2–29 and CamSpec EG20 at ℓ=30–2500. CosmoChord/PolyChord nested sampling explores potentially multimodal posteriors; BOBYQA searches high-likelihood regions for best-fit candidates rather than established detections.

BINGO numerically evaluates primordial spectra for the featureless, step, kink and dark-energy models; the dark-dimension spectrum uses Eq. (2.9). Forecasts fit simulated TT, TE and EE spectra using survey noise, Gaussian beams and an inverted-Wishart likelihood, retaining the data-analysis priors.

The censorship test expands the minimum of f under parameter changes, imposing f′(r_min)=0 and f″(r_min)>0. The analysis also uses dM=dU+p dV+V dP and near-extremal expansions to discuss horizon survival and charge-to-mass conditions.

A minimally coupled charged massive Klein–Gordon equation is separated into e^(−iωt)R_lm(r)Y_lm. The tortoise coordinate satisfies dr/dr*=f; the near-horizon radial equation retains (ω−qΦ_h)² and the ingoing solution is selected.

Energy-momentum and electric-current fluxes are integrated over the horizon using normalized spherical harmonics. Their infinitesimal changes are inserted into thermodynamic and horizon-variation expressions.

Construct rotationally symmetric gauge bundles using sphere tangent or spin bundles, then evaluate characteristic numbers with Chern roots and index-theorem arguments. Nonzero characteristic numbers obstruct smooth bordism fillings through a Stokes-type argument.
Use ordinary and mod-2 elliptic genera, invertible anomaly theories, APS η-invariants, and global Green–Schwarz pairings to detect SQFT classes even after forgetting their gauge symmetry.

Factor current algebras as G1=[Hk×SO(n)1]/(−1)^FL. For n=2,4,8, the tangent-bundle embedding produces an N=(1,1) sphere sigma model. The n=1 argument instead uses T-duality, winding tachyons, and a discrete Arf term.

Construct fixed-t twice-subtracted dispersion relations from a complex-s contour, using s–u crossing and the assumed vanishing contour contribution at infinity. Convert s- and u-channel projectors into a common low-energy color basis.

Find color-space vectors whose singlet component is normalized to one and whose contractions annihilate the proposed ultraviolet support in both crossed channels. If such support were exhaustive, the surviving graviton pole would have to equal an analytic polynomial, yielding a contradiction.

For spin-2 representation tests, use improved dispersion relations retaining finitely many EFT coefficients, forward null constraints, positive spectral densities, and SDPB optimization. Smearing uses weights (1−p)p^n with t=−p².

Fourier-transform the static photon propagator, differentiate the resulting potential to obtain the radial force, and compare that force with Newtonian gravity. Estimate experimental sensitivity by matching the potential modification to a Yukawa parametrization used in Cavendish-type tests.

Review the tree-level electromagnetic vertex charge form factor and its leading non-local correction, match it to anomaly-compatible charge dequantization, and insert the neutrino charge bound into electric-WGC inequalities.

The supergravity construction dualizes a specific combination involving the dilaton multiplet's auxiliary scalar into H2=dB1, then couples a κ-symmetric superparticle. Distributional field equations and Killing-spinor equations determine static wall solutions and preserved supersymmetry.

The compactification analysis combines ten-dimensional Einstein and dilaton equations, RR flux quantization, electric-magnetic dualization, and wrapped-brane stress tensors. Effective particle tensions are identified from curvature backreaction after smearing internal transverse directions.

Superspace changes of variables, Berezinians, and integration by parts establish invariance of the dressed action. An alternative derivation requires dressed supercoordinates Y^M=e^(−δϕ)Z^M to transform as chiral superfields.

The integral BCH formula yields Bernoulli-weighted nested commutators for Stückelberg transformations. Projection to Θ=0 gives component transformation laws, and an order-by-order recursion handles the field-dependent generators.

Finite transformations are obtained by exponentiating combined diffeomorphism and local supersymmetry variations. Their composition uses the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula, retaining variations of the supergravity fields inside the transformation generator.

Holographic renormalization uses Fefferman–Graham expansions and curvature counterterms determined iteratively through a Gauss–Codazzi constraint. Appendix A provides an alternative calculation using asymmetric Shiromizu–Maeda–Sasaki effective brane equations.

Euclidean Coleman–de Luccia instantons, subtraction of parent and instanton actions to obtain the bounce exponent, and Wick rotation of a spherical coordinate to obtain Lorentzian de Sitter evolution.

The N=2 analysis uses symplectic sections, electric-magnetic frame changes, monodromies, and modular third derivatives of the one-loop prepotential. Gauge-enhancement singularities and perturbative asymptotics constrain the resulting modular functions.

N=1 couplings are constrained by Kähler transformations and modular weights. Dedekind η, the invariant j-function, Eisenstein series, and holomorphic versus nonholomorphic regularizations provide explicit superpotentials and threshold corrections.

The species-scale construction combines the attractor mechanism, charge minimization of corrected BPS black-hole entropy, and a nonholomorphic modular completion of the large-volume or weak-coupling F1 expression.

The imported graviton evolution estimate sums near-threshold intra-tower channels, using approximately l δn channels and a daughter velocity proportional to sqrt(mKK δn/ml). It gives Γtot ~ β² δn^(3/2) ml^(7/2)/(Mp² mKK^(1/2)) and a characteristic surviving mass proportional to t^(-2/7).

Entropy conservation is used to estimate the relativistic contribution to ΔNeff from thermally populated light bulk modes, with explicit helicity counting and the entropy degrees of freedom at decoupling.
Weak widths are estimated using Γ(νl→3ν) = GF² ml^5 sin²θl/(192π³), with θl ~ ζ mν/ml. The radiative width is smaller by 27α/(8π). The authors constrain ζ by requiring Γ(νl→γν) ≲ Γ(Gl→γγ).

Abundance contours are combined with the cited Planck isocurvature bound βiso < 0.038 and then mapped from (ma, fa) to (ξ, fa) using the wormhole mass relation. Generic inflation treats the U(1) scalar as a spectator.

Misalignment abundance is calculated separately for oscillation during radiation domination, reheating, or immediately after a thermal phase transition. During radiation domination, entropy conservation gives Ωa h² ≃ 0.12⟨θi²⟩(fa/(7×10^16 GeV))² sqrt(ma/(10^-21 eV)), using g* = g*,s = 106.75.

The authors extend an existing analytic Euclidean wormhole treatment toward the induced-gravity limit. After an Einstein-frame conformal transformation, integrals involving radial kinetic and angular decay functions determine the throat field, throat size Lw and action Sw.

The asymptotic modulus–species relation is substituted into the e-fold count, spectral tilt and tensor ratio. Scalar-amplitude normalization fixes V0 and the inflationary Hubble scale; the resulting cutoff is compared with the observational inputs cited in the paper.

Modular potentials are organized using invariants built from the Dedekind eta function, the modular j-function and an almost-holomorphic weight-two modular form. Their large-τ2 expansion is truncated to V ≃ V0(1 − cn/τ2).
After setting τ2 = exp(aϕ/MPl), the authors use leading slow roll for V ≃ V0[1 − cn exp(−aϕ/MPl)]. Integrating the e-fold count and neglecting its endpoint contribution gives τ2* ≃ a²cn Ne.

For TCOs, introduces A=gϕϕE²+gttL², B=−gϕϕgtt and Veff=ζ+A/B. Circularity requires V−1=0 and its radial derivative to vanish; β determines admissibility. As written, positive second derivative denotes unstable TCOs and negative second derivative stable TCOs.

Numerically studies metric roots, photon-potential extrema and vector-field zeros because the general metric equations are difficult to solve analytically. Reported thresholds and orbit locations are author calculations from selected parameter slices.

Uses a geometry-only photon-sphere potential H, independent of incoming-particle energy and angular momentum. Duan's mapping constructs a normalized two-component gradient field; its zeros locate photon spheres, while winding numbers assign topological charges.

Canonical quantization substitutes momenta by −i times field derivatives and imposes HΨ=0. Appendix B describes diagonalizing the quadratic second-derivative form through a nondegenerate linear transformation, with canonical coefficients drawn from {1,−1,0}.

A reverse Faddeev–Jackiw-inspired construction relates canonical and deformed phase spaces through a linear map x=Mx̃. Restrictions on M retain coordinate polynomial structure and are intended to recover the preceding two-field model when the inflaton field and its momentum vanish.

Reported solution techniques include successive approximations for Ψ(η), Airy functions for Ψ(ξ), and Hermite/confluent-hypergeometric functions for the quadratic-potential Ψ(φ). Numerical solution families and Argand diagrams illustrate selected boundary conditions and both inflation potentials.

Uses the stationary semiclassical equation Ji=Σj(piΓi→j−pjΓj→i)+piΣyΓi→y. Inverting its rate matrix gives a path expansion whose Nth term represents creation followed by N transitions. Small dS-to-dS branching fractions motivate retaining zero and one transition.

Uses thin-wall Coleman–de Luccia decay exponents and parametric domain-wall tensions to estimate decompactification, flux transitions and destruction of the uplift. Appendix calculations distinguish generic branes from near-BPS lower tension bounds.

Compares Euclidean creation instantons for spherical universes, ETW-bounded bubbles of something and the Boundary Proposal. Nontrivial compact topology is treated separately because the spatial-curvature tunneling barrier can disappear.

Formal semiclassical path integral expanded to quadratic order in metric perturbations around background saddle points. A Hartree–Fock mean-field split treats the condensate as a classical source; counterterms are invoked to remove fluctuation contributions.

Boundary analysis adds Gibbons–Hawking–York and axion-dependent extrinsic-curvature CS terms to obtain a Dirichlet variational principle. The authors argue that the relevant quadratic boundary variations vanish and do not cancel the condensate's imaginary parts.

Canonical quantization in the helicity basis, reducing tensor propagation to two scalar modes; composite-operator commutators are evaluated in a Bunch–Davies-type vacuum with UV-cutoff momentum integrals.

Use approximate seesaw diagonalization to express active–sterile mixing through mass eigenvalues, then compare T-mediated proton-decay amplitudes with neutron–sterile mixing amplitudes. Collider lifetimes and disappearance times are estimated at order of magnitude.

Insert the adjoint VEV into higher-dimensional Yukawa operators to exhibit doublet–triplet coupling splitting. Integrate out T at tree level to obtain four-fermion operators with coefficients given by coupling products divided by m_T².

The imported f(R) perturbation formalism retains both Bardeen potentials, modified tensor friction, and a geometric anisotropic source. The authors then argue that this source is negligible in their axion-matter regime, permitting use of the usual GR resonant tensor contribution.

Newtonian-gauge cosmological perturbation theory is used with first-order Bardeen potentials and second-order tensor modes. The GR calculation uses Green functions, scalar transfer functions, and convolution integrals over the primordial scalar power spectrum.

The scalaron is defined by F=df/dR. Rather than numerically solving its massive wave equation, the calculation uses δF=F_R δR and expresses δR through the Bardeen potentials. Scalaron and tensor power contributions are combined into an oscillation-averaged, subhorizon GW abundance and redshifted to today.

Polynomial and Bessel-function smearings produce elastic and inelastic bounds, with Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities used for products of distinct couplings. Large-J asymptotics support positivity; a regulated Bessel limit recovers an impact-parameter/eikonal description.

The graviton 1/t pole prevents a direct forward-limit positivity argument. The authors integrate dispersion relations against smearing functions over negative t, imposing inequalities for every allowed resonance mass and spin. Endpoint zeros cancel crossed-channel singularities when the integration range reaches the relevant mass threshold.

Spinor-helicity amplitudes are expanded at low energy and related to high-energy resonance exchanges through fixed-negative-t Cauchy dispersion relations. Wigner d-functions encode partial waves, with tree-level spectral weights expressed through masses, spins, and squared couplings.

Euclidean world-volume instantons and Wick rotation describe nucleation; the 2-brane world-volume gauge equation is solved explicitly, and sourced bulk Maxwell equations estimate induced screening at nucleation.

Higher-dimensional results use equations of motion, dimensional analysis and scaling of the bounce action, assuming suitable solutions exist. String comparisons use DBI/CS actions, dimensional reduction and canonical normalization.

Imported SEAQT dynamics adds nonlinear entropy-producing dissipation to von Neumann evolution. Entropy-gradient projection orthogonal to the constrained operator manifold, implemented through Gram-Schmidt/Gram determinants, is intended to preserve trace and mean energy.

The authors use a replica-trick entropy expansion, project free-energy contributions onto the graviton and orthogonal sectors, expand perturbation equations to first order, and introduce a local near-equilibrium decomposition F = k_i + G.

Complexify the imported Freedman–Pufu BPS solutions, analyze contours in the complex ρ-plane, and use Fefferman–Graham expansions to select asymptotically real de Sitter geometry and inflaton profiles.

Use holographic renormalization and the finite supersymmetric surface term. The imported regularized action is Ireg(c) = 4π²L²(1−c)/(1+c); the vertical contour supplies divergent counterterms and the cosmological phase.

Modulus–axion cubic interactions are extracted from derivatives ∂τmKnp and transformed into normalized fields. Higgs decays use a Giudice–Masiero coupling. The resulting two-body widths determine visible/hidden branching, reheating and the extra relativistic abundance.

Canonical mixing is obtained from M²=(1/2)K⁻¹V″, solving the mass eigenvector problem with K-metric normalization uᵢᵀKuⱼ=δij. Trace/determinant estimates organize the hierarchical spectrum and approximate mixing separately for small and order-one W0.

Volume extrema are expressed using principal and lower Lambert-W branches. A D-term comparison uses a restricted charge pattern, including Q12=1 and Q21=0 as a simplification, and obtains VD=3d/V² at the transverse minima; the author claims equivalence to the approximate vacuum after parameter rescaling.

Analyze dual tensor/BPS cones, use large-charge supersymmetric black-string attractors to place moduli directions inside the BPS cone, and sequentially blow down −1 generators. Blowdown means approaching an SCFT boundary while retaining its sector, rather than converting a tensor into 29 hypers.

Combine H−V+29T=273 with classified SCFT/LST nodes and links. Interior links including adjacent-node shares contribute at least 27 to the anomaly; repeatable conformal-matter links contribute 30. Sharp rank bounds also use Python numerical optimization of nine semiclassical LST configurations.

Use anomaly inflow and worldsheet unitarity: supergravity strings have cL=3Q²+9b0·Q+2, cR=3Q²+3b0·Q, kL=(Q²−b0·Q+2)/2, and ki=Q·bi. Current algebras consume central charge k dim G/(k+h∨), whose summed contributions cannot exceed cL.

Use a Scherk–Schwarz ansatz with fields twisted by exp[My/(2πR)]. Reduction produces a radion-dependent potential proportional to e^{2(α−β)ϕ} times a trace involving M and the scalar matrix H. For real M, the potential is nonnegative and can vanish when M is conjugate to a rotation generator.

Build twists from diffeomorphisms, B-field shifts and β-transformations. T-duality relates H-, geometric f-, and non-geometric Q-fluxes. Integer fluxes determine parabolic, elliptic or hyperbolic monodromies for the torus moduli.

After elliptic stabilization, reparameterize the remaining runaway variables into radial and angular coordinates and minimize the potential at fixed radial coordinate. The toy construction selects ϑ=π/4; the four-dimensional construction uses the corresponding alignment to obtain the desired power law.

Use Gaussian null coordinates, Raychaudhuri's equation and horizon pullbacks to evaluate canonical energy. Separate gravitational shear, electromagnetic horizon flux and a late-time spacelike contribution, evaluating the last through a reference family of static solutions.

Apply the imported Iyer–Wald off-shell covariant phase-space identities through second order. Integrate over a hypersurface bounded by the background bifurcation surface and the paper's substitute spatial infinity; canonical energy is the integral of the presymplectic current.

Use independent random-phase maps and dominant phase-cancellation patterns to estimate radiation Rényi entropies. Compare ρ with its charge rotation U(a)ρU(a)† through trace-difference and sandwiched Rényi quantities, replica continuation and fidelity.

Construct non-isometric maps by a unitary acting with a fixed auxiliary input, followed by postselection: V=√|P|⟨0|P U|ψ0⟩f, with an analogous W. Haar integration computes average inner products and a fourth-moment fluctuation bound.

Cheeger–Simons differential characters, their products and fibre integration organize the reduction. The cubic M-theory Chern–Simons character supplies anomaly terms; the proposed degree-12 character Ğ4 ⋆ (dG7)̆ supplies BF terms. Nonclosed G7 itself is not refined as an ordinary differential character.

Poincaré duality, torsion linking, Künneth tensor/Tor contributions and toric intersection numbers determine coefficients and brane pairings. A boundary projection/sandwich construction extracts physical topological sectors from the SymTFT.

The photon-sphere method uses H(r,θ)=√(f/h)/sinθ and vector components φr=√g∂rH, φθ=(∂θH)/√h. Zeros and assigned topological charges classify light rings; detailed foundations of charge evaluation are deferred to cited work.

Timelike-orbit classification uses metric combinations A=gφφE²+gttL² and B=−gφφgtt, an effective potential and a β diagnostic. Negative β marks forbidden circular-orbit regions. The model equations are solved numerically because general closed solutions are unavailable.

Construct explicit metric, form-field and factorised-spinor embedding Ansätze using only universal CY3 tensors. Internal spinor projections, Clifford algebra and Fierz identities relate supersymmetry transformations; factorised Hodge duality and CY3 tensor identities reduce the bosonic equations.

Determine fermion bilinear corrections by matching higher- and lower-dimensional supercovariant field strengths and spin connections. Establish consistency through bosonic equations, on-shell supersymmetry transformations, and the remaining nonlinear fermionic equations outlined in Appendix B.

Dimensional reduction and a derivative expansion of the D4 DBI plus Chern-Simons action recover the classical cancellation of tension and flux coupling. Conformal dimensional analysis relates a generated potential to V∝Φ6∝R3.

Chan-Paton orbifold/orientifold projections and Higgs/Coulomb branches determine probe gauge theories. The transverse D4–O6− intersection requires a symplectic projection. Nonperturbative analysis uses imported gauge dynamics and Euclidean D2 fermion-zero-mode counting, including endpoint and tachyon-recombination effects.

Use the three real symmetric SO(10) Yukawa matrices and fermion mass relations to eliminate the original couplings and express neutral-scalar Yukawa matrices through physical masses, CKM mixing, an unknown unitary matrix V_E and coefficients C_FF′.

Construct ratios of efficiency-corrected LFV resonance yields, neutral-meson new-physics contributions and proton partial widths. Combine them with row/column unitarity of V_E to remove nuisance parameters and obtain a leading-order consistency relation.

Evaluate the one-loop partition-function integral numerically over the modular fundamental domain, using its shifted-sector q-expansion. At large radius, use Poisson resummation, strip integration, modified Bessel functions and restricted nonholomorphic Eisenstein sums to characterize the asymptotics.

Implement Scherk-Schwarz breaking through correlated fractional KK shifts and shifts of internal Cartan charges. A sector decomposition with GSO projections preserves modular invariance and connects supersymmetric large-radius and potentially nonsupersymmetric small-radius limits.

Estimate the two-loop energy from representative massless sunset contributions, parameterized by a,b,c and restricted Eisenstein functions and their order derivative. Eliminate the dilaton through its stationary equation, then minimize numerically in T_2,U_2.

Benchmark the same integration procedure against known analytic n=2 six-brane solutions, including their coordinate transformation and extremal Lambert-W representation. Also compare near-extremal numerical throats with the analytic cigar limit.

Construct analytic asymptotic expansions to initialize numerical integrations: retain the mode that decays into the extremal throat, or use an even-power near-horizon expansion ensuring Euclidean smoothness. Monitor the Hamiltonian constraint independently.

Reduce the spherically symmetric supergravity action to a one-dimensional radial Lagrangian and Hamiltonian. Variation of the lapse imposes H=0; fix N=1 and integrate the remaining nonlinear ordinary differential equations.

Transform the equations of motion to the Einstein frame because an effective action for the IFS gas is unavailable. Analyze the attractor by a weak-coupling expansion of the dilaton velocity deviation, and study bounces through reduced equations and a numerical example.

Estimate IFS lifetime from semiclassical splitting, use the local linear-dilaton solution and production rate for short-lived strings, and impose the string-frame Bianchi identity to determine energy transfer. The lifetime estimate leaves an order-one coefficient γ undetermined.

The CY argument uses polarized variations of Hodge structure, the positive Hodge inner product, and stability of invariant subspaces under the operator C to construct invariant complements. Explicit one-parameter volumes are evaluated through Stokes contour integrals of the Kähler potential.

Compactification of all spatial dimensions produces supersymmetric quantum mechanics. Normalizable ground states are identified with L² harmonic forms; cited asymptotic L²-cohomology results then constrain candidate target-space geometries.

Use the imported N=2 JT disc partition function and one-loop determinants, sum over integer electric-holonomy windings, and apply Poisson resummation, inverse Laplace transformation and charge Fourier transformation to obtain multiplet and fixed-charge densities.

Expand the renormalized Euclidean action near the BPS limit in a mixed ensemble, reduce the bosonic theory to two dimensions, and identify linearized dilaton dynamics with JT gravity. Gravitino nearly zero modes are essential to the supersymmetric quantum correction.

Coset harmonic analysis: decompose a field's tangent-space representation into H representations, then select G representations whose restriction to H contains those components. Cross diagrams organize the resulting isometry representations.

Construct all 21 two-form modes by applying operators containing octonionic tensors and Sp1^C Killing vectors to scalar modes; 15 cross diagrams contain transverse modes. Acting with the universal Laplacian on explicit modes ties eigenvalues to isometry representations. One construction includes a symmetrized two-derivative operator.

Use the relation between coset structure constants and octonionic structure constants to construct a G2-covariant derivative. A universal Laplacian unifies the form and Lichnerowicz operators; solving its equations requires G2 projectors expressed through octonionic tensors.

Use the ADM time-space split and Henneaux–Teitelboim Hamiltonian formulation. Only spatial two-form components enter the action; the Poincaré lemma integrates their Euler–Lagrange equations to the duality equations, introducing temporal components as integration data.

Use superconformal tensor calculus and the Bergshoeff–de Roo map: identify a torsionful spin connection, gravitino curvature and auxiliary curvature with an off-shell Yang–Mills multiplet. Pull back its invariant through an embedding valid modulo two-derivative equations. The perturbative Noether/BV discussion permits field redefinitions, subject to stated complications.

Use plane-wave and Fourier ansätze, characteristic equations with vanishing discriminant, a self-dual electromagnetic sector and a momentum-space propagator matrix. Linearized axion and photon equations are then cast into a two-component Schrödinger-like propagation equation.

Vary the proposed Lagrangians with respect to torsion and axions, eliminate the algebraically related trace vector, and impose S=∂φ or S=∂a to express torsion effects through scalar dynamics and masses.

Linearize the photon equations and use a Lorenz-gauge ansatz with transverse harmonic components. Polarization one is perpendicular to the impact parameter, while polarization two is parallel; the transverse family shares one delay independently of its free polarization parameters.

Take distributional ultraboost limits and extract Δv from ∂u∂vΦ + Δvδ(u)∂v²Φ = 0. Outside the usual mass/charge scaling limit, impose positivity on the leading divergent delay rather than require a finite delay.

Review functional-constraint implementations of torsion conservation and the three-form Bianchi identity, followed by path integration over nonpropagating torsion or the three-form. This yields an axion coupled to the gravitational Pontryagin density.

The reviewed condensate calculation uses canonical quantization of weak gravitational waves in TT gauge, a quadratic gravitational-wave path integral and Hartree–Fock mean field. The leptogenesis estimate imports analytical Padé-approximant treatment of freezeout.

Twisted differential cohomology implements a torsional Kaluza–Klein expansion. Hamiltonian brane commutators and flux non-commutativity determine quadratic couplings; reduction of the M-theory effective action supplies the cubic coupling.
M5 dressings are extracted using an auxiliary seven-dimensional functional encoding dh3=G4. Continuous anomaly inflow uses an RP4 fibration, global angular forms, and Bott–Cattaneo fiber integration.
Background-metric expansion, covariant de Donder and noncovariant Prentki gauges, spin-projector inversion of propagators, and Faddeev–Popov gauge fixing.
The functional RG supplies a formally exact nonperturbative flow equation. String low-energy actions are obtained through worldsheet anomaly cancellation and S-matrix matching.
S-matrix analyticity, dispersion/arc integrals, partial-wave unitarity and moment inequalities constrain EFT coefficients; eikonal resummation estimates graviton-mediated Regge behavior.

Nonperturbative tools discussed include integrability, AdS/CFT and functional RG. Loll's contribution advocates CDT lattice path integrals and Monte Carlo computations of diffeomorphism-invariant observables.

Reviewed amplitude methods extend Einstein-Hilbert gravity by EFT couplings, use on-shell unitarity and Kawai-Lewellen-Tye gauge-gravity relations, and extract classical compact-object observables through post-Minkowskian expansions, including relativistic velocities.

Semiclassical saddle-point methods and gravitational path integrals are considered bridges beyond EFT. Relevant saddles, sums over topology, spacetime signature and Wick rotation remain debated rather than fixed components of a common prescription.

Track time-dependent warp factors through M-theory, IIB and IIA configurations, then an M-theory uplift. Blowing up two orbifold singularities leaves the Horava-Witten walls; shrinking their interval motivates the heterotic endpoint.

Dimensionally reduce the heterotic Einstein-frame three-form action, impose its Bianchi identity with a Lagrange multiplier, integrate out H3 and introduce an axion through a temporal integral. The time-dependent kinetic factor produces additional interactions.

RR flow equations are motivated by supergravity equations of motion. The short-time argument uses DeTurck gauge fixing, linearization, the Weitzenböck identity and parabolic PDE theory, followed by undoing the gauge transformation.

Variational gradient-flow construction from F = ∫e^(−f)dV_g [R − |H|²/12 + |∇f|²], subject to a weighted-volume constraint; an ∇f-generated diffeomorphism decouples f from the NSNS metric and B-field equations.

Condensation is implemented by a fine Wilson-line mesh, assigning ρ0(p) to each internal line and C0(pi,pj,pk) to each trivalent junction. Fusion and modular-S kernel identities, braiding, and Wilson bubble/triangle reductions simplify the mesh into projectors and factorized states.

Generalized Heegaard splitting decomposes manifolds into compression bodies. Complete conformal-block states are inserted on inner boundaries, and outer states are glued using their inner product, optionally twisted by a mapping-class operator.

CYTools and an inherited-orientifold construction supply geometric data. Most ensemble models lie on the ray through the stretched Kähler-cone tip, with homogeneous dilation selecting points satisfying the mass and gauge-coupling criteria.

Misalignment abundances are computed numerically from the onset condition 3H(z_a)≈m_a and subsequent matter-like redshifting. Individual abundances are added instead of solving coupled axion equations; resonant energy transfer is deferred.

Joint cosmological inference uses Planck 2018 temperature, polarization and lensing, BAO, and Pantheon+ supernovae, with MontePython, MultiNest, and AxiCLASS. Cosmological and nuisance parameters are varied and marginalized.

Use anomaly inflow and an imported supergravity-string worldsheet constraint: kIJ(p)=FIJK p^K has one positive eigenvalue, r−1 negative eigenvalues and potentially null directions. Strings have an N=(0,4) worldsheet theory flowing to an infrared SCFT; bulk inflow must cancel its anomalies.

Apply Lorentzian lightcone arguments and Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities, with projections to nondegenerate anomaly subspaces, to constrain cubic couplings. Combine F=1 with asymptotic scaling and cancellation bounds for fIJ; ranks of its leading submatrices count the fastest weakly coupled one-form combinations.

Asymptotic Hodge theory supplies nilpotent-orbit periods Π_nil=exp(zN)a_0. The authors construct the potential using an sl(2) approximation to the Hodge norm/Weil operator, retaining integral fluxes and algebraic saxion dependence.

A k-nearest-neighbors classifier, with k=5, learns parameter regions labelled by γ_uplift<1 at nine selected field-space points. This is a preliminary exclusion/search filter for candidate valleys, rather than a test of complete inflationary dynamics.
Numerical parameter scans locate positive complex-structure minima. Candidate valleys are obtained from ∂_s V(a,s_v(a))=0; the function s_v(a) measures saxion backreaction as the axion is displaced.

Integrate out the bulk gauge components using their equations of motion and brane boundary conditions. Express the remaining field through a gauge-invariant Wilson loop to obtain the radion-dependent axion kinetic term.

Solve the radial string equation numerically and compare with a matched approximation joining small- and large-radius solutions. Integrate the energy density separately over the core and exterior, retaining the global-string infrared logarithm.

The analysis uses small-x series, exact ansätze for special couplings, and first-order perturbations near b=a or a=1. The perturbation near b=a is integrated using an integrating factor and expressed through a hypergeometric function.

Large-radius expansions produce an Einstein constraint relating mass, electromagnetic charges and scalar charges. Symmetry dependence on asymptotic scalar values, an imported first-law relation for scalar charges, and degree-one mass homogeneity reduce that constraint to a first-order mass ODE.
For a=b, a U(1) subgroup of the enhanced SL(2,R) symmetry rotates an imported purely electric or magnetic Gibbons–Maeda solution into a dyonic EMDA solution with nonzero axion.

Express momenta in dual scaled root/weight bases, form their Gram matrices, and package pL²±pR² as quadratic forms on integer momentum/winding vectors. Construct genus-one partition functions as lattice Gaussian sums.

Use a differential equation relating the upper-half-plane and Narain-moduli Laplacians, followed by moduli integration, modular covariance and Eisenstein-series asymptotics to characterize the proposed average.

The authors diagonalize the RHN mass matrix, apply the type-I seesaw for mD below the heavy masses, and use Casas–Ibarra parametrization with a complex orthogonal angle θR to obtain neutrino Yukawas consistent with oscillation inputs.

Majoron abundance is obtained from a temperature-dependent Boltzmann equation for NiNi → χχ, using equilibrium RHN yields and a thermally averaged annihilation cross-section, integrated from TRH to the present temperature.

Unflavored leptogenesis is treated through coupled RHN-abundance and lepton-asymmetry Boltzmann equations, including decays, inverse decays and Higgs-mediated ΔL = 1 scatterings. The CP asymmetry includes vertex and self-energy interference contributions.
Compare global minimum χ² using the Procoli simulated-annealing optimizer and estimate Bayesian evidence with MCEvidence. Profile likelihoods supplement the marginalized posterior analysis.
Implement the background and perturbation model in modified CLASS, sample with MontePython MCMC using Cholesky parameter decomposition, require Gelman–Rubin R−1<0.01, and analyze chains with GetDist.

Assess SH0ES compatibility with QDMAP=√[χ²min(D+MB)−χ²min(D)]. Because the formula assumes one added degree of freedom, the authors use Pantheon+ plus a Gaussian MB calibration prior solely for this diagnostic.

Auxiliary fields resolve the double-trace deformation in the path integral. Large-N saddle-point variation yields mixed conditions Φ̂(s) + w + vΠ(b) = 0 and Φ̂(b) + vΠ(s) = 0, where Π is the on-shell action derivative with respect to the boundary field.

Constrained maximization of von Neumann entropy gives a product coarse-grained state: ρ̄(s) ∝ exp[−β(H*(s) − μO)] and ρ̄(b) ∝ exp[−BH*(b)]. Multipliers reproduce the exact state's accessible expectation values; O need not commute with H*(s).

Examples solve the scalar response on BTZ at O(λ), include metric backreaction at O(λ²), and construct auxiliary Euclidean black holes matching energy. Thermal CFT Kubo-response calculations and retarded Green's functions provide the boundary treatment.

Nonlinear sigma models describe Goldstone Higgs fields; symmetry completion with gauge or fermion partners regulates explicit breaking. Extra-dimensional examples use Einstein–Hilbert reduction, Weyl transformations and dimensional deconstruction.

Spurion representations, dimensional analysis and scale-separated expansions organize symmetry breaking and UV sensitivity. Treating ℏ as dimensionful supplies loop counting; the scalar example combines this with traceless rank-six tensors to infer that their wavefunction-renormalization contribution first appears at four loops.

Superspace, holomorphic superpotentials, symmetry selection rules and elimination of auxiliary F and D fields construct supersymmetric theories. The review explains non-renormalization through holomorphy while retaining Kähler and wavefunction renormalization.

Generalized field coordinates and a position-space Lorentz representation translate the map to Dirac fields. The mass-to-spin-connection argument uses spatial projection, integration by parts, chiral decomposition and vielbeins with a torsionless connection.

Hodge decomposition, Lorentz-generator algebra and the spinor realization xi=ψ†σiψ implement the spin-orbit map. Euclidean continuation relates concentric S³ slices to the Hopf fibration S¹→S³→S²; the free CBS superparticle supplies an explicit realization.

Euclidean free-fermion determinants are evaluated with dimensional regularization in R4 and spectral zeta functions plus heat-kernel subtraction on the cylinder and AdS4. The AdS calculation selects regular discrete modes through conformal-boundary conditions.

Misalignment densities are propagated using conserved comoving particle number N = ρa^3/m in adiabatic evolution. The ALP density at resonance is transferred to the QCD axion and subsequently redshifted to obtain the enhanced relic abundance.

The author diagonalizes the small-amplitude two-field mass matrix into heavy and light eigenstates and defines the resonance temperature by the minimum squared-mass splitting. For fA much larger than fa, the resonance approximately satisfies ma(TR) = mA.

Numerical shooting varies χ(0) with χ′(0)=0, using adaptive DOP853 integration. Critical profiles are tested through tail exponents, regulated L2 norms, the scaling constraint and cutoff dependence of free energy; the detailed numerical convergence study is restricted to d=8.

Action rescalings yield an instability bound and generalized on-shell scaling constraints. Near Hagedorn, the leading temperature-dependent potential is related to the Hagedorn potential by V1 = (m∞^2 α′/κ)∂φV0; a scaling integral provides a necessary test for normalizable solutions.

Spherical equations are rewritten as generalized Emden–Fowler equations with X = e^(2x)χ and e^x = r√(κ/α′). The resulting friction coefficient d−7 helps classify bounded profiles and their possible r^−2 or r^(3−d) tails.

Reviewed amplitude tools include recursion relations and the amplituhedron in idealized supersymmetric settings, plus color-kinematics duality and double copy connecting gauge-theory and gravitational scattering. Their role is to provide structural insights relevant to difficult precision calculations.

Cobordism theory is reported as a tool for checking local and global anomalies of nonsupersymmetric strings. Symmetry TFTs are reviewed as tools for classifying phases and phase transitions with categorical symmetries.

The review describes reconstruction of AdS string amplitudes using conformal bootstrap, supersymmetric localization, integrability and number theory. Proposed curvature corrections are represented by worldsheet-type integrals with single-valued polylogarithm insertions.

The authors evaluate gauge-anomaly sums and identify the physical axion by orthogonality to eaten Goldstone modes and massive pseudoscalars. Domain-wall numbers are calculated from the minimum positive integer allowed by the axion’s component periodicities.

Quality estimates minimize the QCD plus gravity-induced potentials in the small-shift approximation. Explicit one- and three-loop estimates test induced scalar operators; Model I uses M* as the cutoff of quadratically divergent loops. The SO(10) phenomenology also uses numerical VEV scans.

Black-hole entropy consistency motivates a species cutoff Λ_s=1/l_min. Higher-curvature terms are controlled by this scale, and the review imposes the Planck-unit EFT validity condition V≲Λ_s² to constrain positive potentials.

For one scalar, the review combines the d-dimensional Friedmann equation, scalar equation of motion, positive kinetic energy and V>0 with the TCC integral bound on ∫Hdt, obtaining restrictions on H, V and field excursions.

Modified FortEPiaNO simultaneously evolves scalar decay, total-energy continuity and momentum-dependent neutrino density matrices, including collisions and flavor oscillations. After decoupling, spectra are converted to mass eigenstates using fνi=Σα|Uαi|²fνα.

Modified CLASS and MontePython interpolate neutrino spectra on a reheating-temperature grid and sample six ΛCDM parameters plus TRH. BBN consistency supplies Yp(TRH,ωb) from PArthENoPE; the reference CMB calculation retains the full nonthermal spectra.

Modified PArthENoPE uses the computed neutrino energy density and electron-neutrino spectrum, with radiative corrections applied consistently to modified Born weak rates throughout BBN. The adopted neutron lifetime is (879.4±0.6) s.

Canonical quantization uses first-order gravitational variables, a restricted connection phase space enforcing invertibility, and Hamiltonian reduction. The remaining quantum constraints are identified with Virasoro Ward identities.

A TQFT folding construction and analytic continuation of the AdS slab amplitude motivate the Liouville wavefunction. Factorization, crossing symmetry and normalizability provide a separate bootstrap motivation.

The previously established complex-Liouville-string matrix description supplies a spectral curve and topological recursion for resolvents. The proposed entropy count integrates the eigenvalue density, equivalently a cycle determining the first ZZ-instanton tension.

The c-map reduces D=4 vector multiplets on a circle and dualizes the D=3 vectors into scalars, producing QK geometry from special Kähler geometry. Its string interpretation is IIA/IIB T-duality; the input prepotential is homogeneous of degree two, with classical cubic coefficients supplied by CY triple intersections.

The review invokes the hyperkähler-cone description to establish that the universal-hypermultiplet deformation remains QK. It also describes the r-map from D=5 real special to D=4 special Kähler geometry in the construction of complete targets.

Insert the exact exponential-potential power-law solution, express the kinetic-to-potential ratio in terms of λ, and obtain the rational inequality (30). The authors report the cubic test f(λ)≤0 in Eqs. (31)–(32). With A=4(d−1)/(d−2), for d>2 the branch condition ε<d−1 gives A−λ²>0. Multiplying the rational inequality by this denominator yields a cubic with linear term −Aλ, whereas the printed test has −Aκ_d²λ. The checked equivalence therefore holds for κ_d²=1 within that domain. General-κ normalization is flagged for coordinator inspection without changing the printed formula.

Integrate the higher-dimensional SEC inequality over the internal manifold, use the normalized warped-volume identity, and substitute the effective Einstein and scalar equations to express the acceleration restriction as a potential-derivative bound.
Dimensional reduction of λΦ²ΨcΨ/M*² gives M = πRM*²/(2λ) and exhibits equal Weinberg-type couplings of the scalar zero mode to the neutrino tower.

Cutoff estimates of one-loop Higgs quartic and two-loop Higgs mass diagrams isolate tower enhancement. Parametrically, |δλ| scales as N(Λ/M)²/(8π²), while the two-loop mass correction scales as NΛ²(Λ/M)²/(8π²)²; channel constants are not fixed.

A time-dependent orthogonal rotation aligns one direction with the background velocity and rotates the remaining field directions into a semikinematic entropy basis. Applying the rotation and its time derivatives yields coupled equations for Ql, δs1 and δs2.

To preserve independent vacuum fluctuations, the perturbation system is solved three times, exciting one Bunch–Davies mode while setting the others to zero. Contributions to two-point functions are added, rather than initializing all modes as one coherent solution.

Background and perturbation ODEs are solved numerically. Evolution begins at Ne=−80 and ends at Ne=0; spectra and cross-correlations are evaluated for modes exiting during the final 60 e-folds, with −60 to −50 associated with CMB scales.

Double holography relates bulk gravity, a half-space CFT_d/BCFT_{d−1} system, and an intermediate description with cutoff CFT_d coupled to AdS_d gravity. The intermediate theory couples to the nongravitating half-space theory through transparent boundary conditions.

Explicit tools include Fefferman–Graham expansions and holographic renormalization for the induced brane action, plus anomaly-polynomial descent and higher-dimensional inflow for anomalous localized symmetries.

Uniform radial solutions use shooting. Non-uniform solutions use relaxation on compactified radial and half-period Lobatto–Chebyshev grids, seeded by localized higher-dimensional solutions and continued in m∞L.
Solve the leading HP field equations and a quartic-corrected action. The quartic interactions are imported from string scattering amplitudes for bosonic and type II strings.
For d=6, introduce cos(2πz/L) perturbations of a uniform solution. Normalizability gives an eigenvalue problem for L; the resulting perturbation seeds nonlinear relaxation.

Use asymptotic unbiased estimation, classical/quantum Fisher information and Kraus-gauge channel bounds. An explicit gauge yields β̂=0 and an operator-norm optimization; minimax and purification convert this bound into optimization over initial states. Semidefinite programs supply numerical optima.

Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization places the initial state and its noise images before signal images, separating noisy and noise-free subspaces. Compute the projector using a Gram-matrix inverse or Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse when noise images are dependent. For commuting Hermitian jumps, optimization reduces to real vectors and probability distributions.

Solve the extremal boundary-value problem independently by shooting and modified gradient flow, with reported agreement. Integrate nonextremal solutions outward from a regular horizon, fit their vacuum asymptotics, and obtain temperature from Euclidean conical regularity.

Reduce the Einstein equations using radial metric ansätze and their first-order constraint. The extremal radial equation admits a mechanical interpretation with friction and an effective potential U; the nonextremal equations determine B and R before reconstructing A.

For charged massive fields, approximate a potential maximum near the event horizon, apply WKB under a large-mass/large-coupling hierarchy, and combine the resulting charge-to-mass condition with an assumed weak gravity bound. Extremal background relations are obtained from f(r)=f′(r)=0.

Integrate the wave equation on a double-null finite-difference grid. Prony fitting represents the signal as a finite sum of damped complex exponentials, solves a polynomial for modal roots and obtains ωj=i log(zj)/h. Compare extracted neutral-field results with WKB.

Separate the Klein–Gordon equation into spherical harmonics and a radial equation using a tortoise coordinate. Compute quasinormal frequencies with a potential-barrier WKB expansion, including displayed higher-order corrections.
Reviews numerical construction of the PBH-producing potential, log-normal fits to scalar and induced-GW spectra, and a cited δN calculation of quantum-loop corrections.

Uses Legendre–Weyl transformation and inverse parametric reconstruction between scalar potentials and F(R), a left Painlevé series for the background, and slow-roll expansions in inverse e-fold number.

Use the imported gravity/saddle relation a=h2/(πα′), ρ=2h1/(πα′) along constant h2^D to identify densities. Generalized Lambert functions and coordinate changes reduce their moments to contour residues.
Supersymmetric localization on S⁴ or HS⁴, with an equatorial S³ interface/boundary and pole insertions, reduces the problem to matrix integrals evaluated on large-N saddle densities.

Remove curvature-induced mixing using defect-free SYM Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization, Chebyshev-polynomial single-trace insertions and a finite-N normal-ordering algorithm retaining leading multi-trace contributions.

Fix finite counterterms through subtraction conditions at q_star, impose M_grav(0)=M_Pl, and infer running from reference-scale independence. RG improvement sets q_star=q only at the end; strong coupling is estimated from the running coupling reaching unity.

Compute the scalar bubble and quartic-vertex loop diagrams using dimensional regularisation and Feynman parametrisation. Renormalise the graviton kinetic term and curvature-squared operators; the authors report Ward-identity checks throughout.

Modular transformations and chemical-potential periodicities of the flavored torus partition function generate spectral flow; an extended charged Cardy formula is then used to discuss charge bounds and state densities.

Normalized integration over moduli space with its Zamolodchikov measure, the Siegel–Weil relation between averaged theta functions and Eisenstein series, and a Roelcke–Selberg description of departures from that relation.

Linearize the ten-dimensional equations and Bianchi identities, first for static deformations and then for spacetime-dependent moduli. Construct the quadratic action from fluctuations contracted with linearized EOM operators; impose constraints off shell while retaining dynamical operators.

Use Hodge decomposition, the partial–partial-bar lemma, and Poisson equations to determine flux potentials, warp-factor changes, and metric compensators. Solutions are expressed formally through biscalar and bivector Green’s functions.

Combine the leading gravitational term -f_lambda times each quartic coupling with imported two-loop large-N matter beta functions. Solve the resulting algebraic fixed-point equations and analyze stability-matrix eigenvalues and RG trajectories.

Use the functional renormalization group with the Wetterich equation, a Litim regulator and a linear background-metric split. Project the flow onto the scalar two-point momentum term and constant-field quartic interactions to extract anomalous dimensions and gravitational corrections.

Compare brane energy leakage with expansion cooling, KK energy density during BBN, and the thermal relic density with today's critical density. Separately confront the resulting upper normalcy temperature with reheating lower limits inferred from neutrino thermalization, BBN and cosmological data.

Apply higher-dimensional Schwarzschild-radius, entropy and Hawking-lifetime scalings to six-dimensional PBHs. Graviton-emission recoil supplies the proposed mechanism for a PBH initially on the brane to enter the bulk.

Estimate gravitational intra-tower decays using daughter masses satisfying ml = ml′ + ml″ + ε, with ε ≤ mKKδ and δ of order unity. Channel counting and near-threshold phase space give a characteristic surviving KK mass scaling as t^(-2/7). For n = 2, nearly parallel daughter momenta are argued to keep the channel counting effectively one-dimensional.

Add the long-range interaction matrix to the vacuum and standard matter Hamiltonians. Changes in oscillation probabilities are propagated to prospective detection rates. A null-interaction data assumption produces upper bounds; nonzero true potentials illustrate discovery-related degeneracies.

For the displayed joint parameter regions, minimize the test statistic over the stated uncertainty ranges and both test mass orderings. Compare DUNE, T2HK and their combination in the potential–δCP and potential–sin²θ23 planes at 2σ and 3σ.

Construct Yukawa-type potentials sourced by electrons for Le−Lβ and neutrons for Lμ−Lτ. Sum contributions from Earth, Moon, Sun, Milky Way and cosmological matter, evaluating the average potential at detection. The mediator range determines which source contributions are effective.

Average predicted flavor fractions equally over neutrinos and antineutrinos because the detector does not distinguish them, and average over 25 TeV–2.8 PeV. Compare with the eight-year IceCube HESE plus through-going-muon flavor estimate and prospective 15-year IceCube plus 10-year Gen2 measurements.

Form a posterior for the long-range potential by integrating the flavor-composition likelihood over mixing angles and δCP with Gaussian priors centered on adopted best fits. Use a uniform potential prior on [10^(-24),10^(-16)] eV and extract upper limits labeled 95% C.L.; then translate these into coupling–mediator-mass contours.

Add vacuum, standard charged-current matter and long-range terms to the propagation Hamiltonian. Diagonalize it to obtain an effective mixing matrix Um, use averaged probabilities P̄αβ = Σi|Umαi|²|Umβi|², and map source fractions to Earth fractions.

Compute potential slow-roll predictions and compare with published ns–r contours. For R² inflation, use a higher-dimensional Weyl transformation and canonical scalar normalization to obtain the Einstein-frame potential.
Linearize Einstein equations in comoving gauge E=Fm=δϕ=0. Combine scalar perturbations into Θ and Ω, transform to Mukhanov–Sasaki equations, and use Hankel solutions for scalar and tensor modes.
Sum compact Kaluza–Klein modes through Sν. Gamma-function integral representations, Poisson resummation and modified Bessel functions give asymptotic spectra for b0k≪1 and b0k≫1.
The horizon-polynomial discriminant delineates the RNdS mass–charge 'sharkfin' domain. Potential profiles are examined across that domain and at near-extremal, near-Nariai and lukewarm benchmarks.

An imported modified WKB approach, motivated by Borel resummation and anharmonic-oscillator correspondence, expands ω in inverse powers of L=√[ℓ(ℓ+1)]. Potential derivatives through sixth order determine coefficients while parameters remain symbolic; Im(ω−2)=0 identifies the critical mass.

Analyze four-graviton amplitudes normalized to the two-derivative tree amplitude, using known supersymmetry-protected coefficients, the string genus expansion, and Type IIA/M-theory duality to identify the scales behind individual contributions.

Use topological-string couplings, a generalized holomorphic prepotential and corrected attractor equations to study the protected black-hole entropy index. The explicit D0-tower resummation follows prior work identified by the authors.

Use worldline one-loop amplitudes with KK states, Schwinger proper-time integrals, Epstein ζ-functions and Poisson resummation to determine UV convergence and threshold scaling. Resum massive thresholds into higher-dimensional massless nonanalytic terms.

Solve uncertainty inequalities, select a branch, identify position uncertainty with a horizon diameter, and apply the area law and surface-gravity temperature at the resulting horizon. Rearrange residual factors into matching equations whose solutions are examined.
Solve the horizon equation, express mass and ε through entropy, differentiate at fixed mass, and compare ∂MN/∂ε against the Nariai limit of −T(∂S/∂ε)M.

Uses horizon-scaling wall evolution, a scalar kink for wall tension, pressure balance for annihilation, and a quadrupole GW template calibrated with imported lattice results. The modeled GW spectrum has infrared f^3 and ultraviolet f^-1 slopes.

Imports spherical thin-shell trajectories in General Relativity and percolation estimates of large closed-wall fractions. Late horizon entry determines PBH and baby-universe thresholds; Schwarzschild and de Sitter geometries describe the latter.

Apply that diagnostic to holographic spectral data, flux quantization and the axio-dilaton/gauge-coupling correspondence. Separately use black-hole production and Hawking evaporation to argue that asymptotic field values remain visible in flat-space high-energy scattering.
