The LN-chain format includes cell format, chain length, polynomial degrees and coefficient norms, and the supremum of chain functions; take an integer upper bound. Logical conjunctions/unions contribute max(F₁,F₂)+1, while projections/quantifiers add 1.

Cover the base with three punctured discs and three regular discs; map period images into a fundamental domain using finitely many monodromy transformations, then combine local graph formats and optimize radii.

Construct Log-Noetherian differential chains from Picard–Fuchs equations after separating periods into bounded holomorphic and multivalued factors. Treat logarithmic factors using the real Pfaffian extension R_LN,PF.

Use m_i²L²=Δ_i(Δ_i−d) and the effective cubic combination c′_ijk=c_ijk+(m_i²−m_j²−m_k²)d_ijk/2. Gamma functions in the three-point Witten integral exhibit poles when Θ_i=(Δ_j+Δ_k−Δ_i)/2 is a nonpositive integer.

Compare bulk large-c diagram counting with CFT factorization and single-/double-trace mixing. For DGKT, expand the Kähler-derived kinetic terms and potential to cubic order, canonically normalize fluctuations, diagonalize masses, and extract c′.

Stress-tensor Ward identities and interface OPEs establish the displacement's limiting transformation law. The imported averaged null energy bound ND ≥ 2|c1−c2| removes the anomalous fourth-order pole as ND→0; primary and descendant candidates are then classified.

Conformal constraints on correlators of bulk operators at reflected positions relate displacement insertions to dimension differences. The supplement separately uses displacement Ward identities, regulated integrated correlators, counterterms and an RG beta function to constrain interface-only deformations.

Hamilton–Jacobi functions generate Wheeler–DeWitt states. For the stated ordering, exp(iS1) is an exact minisuperspace solution; Fourier transforms, Gaussian superpositions and stationary phase construct semiclassical packets. Horizon thermodynamics uses averaging after transformation to extrinsic-curvature variables.

Canonical normalization and mass-matrix diagonalization of supergravity effective actions; AdS mass–dimension relations determine spectra, while bulk Witten diagrams determine OPE coefficients and double-trace anomalous dimensions.

A fixed-t analytic dispersion relation expresses the low-energy coefficient c2(t) as s- and u-channel contributions when b2(t)=0. The universal graviton pole contributes −8πGN/t, ensuring a nonzero coefficient near the forward limit and hence at least one exchanged state.

The constructive algorithm alternates elastic scattering with symmetry operations. Weyl reflections, allowed outer automorphisms and imported weight-string relations generate further weights; recursively enlarged polytopes and induction establish coverage of charge sectors.

Gravitino masses diagnose preserved supersymmetry, while scalar spectra assess perturbative stability within half-maximal supergravity. For compatible projected flux sectors, real N=1 superpotentials are obtained from the surviving gravitino mass.

Embedding-tensor quadratic constraints impose the relevant Jacobi and source-free Bianchi identities. Dilaton/flux rescalings move candidate extrema to R=S=T=U=i; Singular's GTZ primary decomposition separates the polynomial system into analytically solved branches.

Explicit type IIB dimensional reduction constructs curvature, gauge-flux and source contributions to the potential. Matching to gauged supergravity requires both the moduli dictionary and substitution of the source Bianchi identities.

CMB-A combines Planck temperature/polarization with joint Planck PR4–ACT DR6 lensing. CMB-B adds SPT-3G spectra and lensing. Fits combine these with DESI DR2 or SDSS BAO, Pantheon+, and optionally its SH0ES calibration.

Modified CLASS evolves backgrounds and linear perturbations; HyRec consistently updates binding energies, scattering cross sections, and recombination coefficients using dynamical me(χ). Nonlinear matter-power corrections use halofit.

Cobaya uses adaptive Metropolis–Hastings MCMC with dragging and flat priors; GetDist produces marginalized constraints. SH0ES runs widen coupling priors from g∈[−0.3,0.3], ζ∈[−0.2,0.2] to g∈[−0.8,0.8], ζ∈[−0.4,0.4].
Join conjugate ket-ket and bra-bra wormholes and integrate over the unobservable universe. The Gaussian trace changes the observed kernel from αk to αk−βk²/αk, with αk=2Re(ak), βk=2Re(bk).

Sum normalised Hartle–Hawking and effective-wormhole contributions with relative topological suppression e^(−SdS). Products of mode determinants set saddle weights; Fourier sums give spatial correlations for the two observation protocols.

Solve scalar equations with Euclidean-cap regularity or two-boundary Dirichlet data, using associated Legendre or hypergeometric functions. On-shell actions reduce to quadratic boundary terms whose imaginary coefficients determine Gaussian correlators.

Construct a Hermitian hard-mode Hamiltonian on positive-norm states with |k|>E. Finite counterterms adjust masses, velocities and Lorentz-breaking corrections; its optical theorem supplies the unitarity input.

Use smeared twice-subtracted arcs, fixed-t or crossing-symmetric dispersion relations, Legendre partial waves and semidefinite optimization. Admissible functionals require nonnegative UV weights for every partial wave, every s≥M² and every relevant channel.

Analytically continue Weinberg soft factors using once-subtracted dispersion relations in QED and twice-subtracted relations in gravity. Their physical-threshold cuts have no pseudothreshold discontinuity.

Insert delta-function constraints and Fourier multipliers into the path integral. Constraints proportional to disk and horizon areas supply localized stress tensors, making the C-metric a saddle of a doubly constrained action. With the chosen normalization, λd=λh=−i/G; multiplier contours are shifted accordingly.

Apply a constrained saddle approximation, sum over Chern sectors, and integrate over R and χ2 with a Jacobian and an unevaluated one-loop determinant. Seven collective coordinates describe four translations and three orientations of the black hole loop.

Regularize conical defects using smooth functions approaching step functions. Evaluate boundary terms at infinity: the gravitational term vanishes after subtraction of the flat reference geometry, and the electromagnetic term vanishes in the asymptotic limit.

Use O(4)-invariant Euclidean bounces for the decoupled, effectively zero-temperature sector and three-dimensional static bounces for the thermal regime. Thin-wall estimates are supplemented by reported FindBounce calculations of the action scalings.

Represent classical bubbles as coherent states, count distributions of constituent occupation among flavor modes, and project over the O(N) group to construct invariant bubble states. At large N and occupation, Stirling estimates give the parametric microstate entropy.

Source a linear transverse-traceless gravitational field with the quantum expectation value of the stress tensor. When each merger branch remains approximately classical, discard off-diagonal stress-tensor matrix elements and express the radiation as a weighted sum over classical merger branches.

Reduce the static spherical ansatz to radial equations using φ=Φ−Σ/2−nσ/2, fix N=1 and Aτ=0, and impose the Hamiltonian constraint. The analytic construction restricts to σ=0 and selects the branch increasing outward from a horizon at τ=0.

Linearize the SU(2) gauge perturbation, separate w=f(τ)e^(−iωt̃), and transform the endpoint equations to Schrödinger form. The arguments use a positive potential at zero added charge and an asymptotic attractive inverse-square potential at the extremal endpoint.
Uses the scalar dictionary m²L²=Δ(Δ−d), conserved-current correlators with CJ proportional to 1/g², and positivity/convexity arguments for charged-operator spectra and OPE coefficients.
Combines area-plus-bulk entanglement entropy, the entanglement first law, relative entropy positivity, a Fisher-information representation of the field-space metric, and quantum focusing.
Employs a domain-wall metric and holographic superpotential W to express Einstein–scalar dynamics as first-order flows, then compares proposed bounds with RG monotonicity and the boundary a-theorem.

Numerically integrates covariant background equations and two independent scalar mode functions using the exact reduced metric and quartic potential. The scalar mass matrix includes the covariant Hessian, field-space curvature, and gravitational constraints. Scalar and tensor modes start in Bunch–Davies states at k/(aH) = 100 and evolve to inflation's end.

Uses the imported refined de Sitter conjecture for V > 0: either ceff = MP‖∇V‖/V ≥ cdS or the smallest eigenvalue ηmin of (MP²/V)G⁻¹∇∇V obeys ηmin ≤ −c′dS. The positive coefficients are conjecturally order unity; the diagnostics are coordinate covariant.

For cosmology, estimate the gCS condensate using quadratic quantum tensor perturbations and use a dynamical-system treatment of the axion and background. Real and imaginary condensate components are assigned inflationary and metastability roles respectively.

Estimate production with interaction kernels and Bogoliubov coefficients. Detector-accessible states require tracing over unobserved directions; covariance matrices illustrate the exact thermal reduction of a two-mode squeezed state.

Expand g=g_background+κh in transverse-traceless gauge through quadratic tensor interactions, quantize finite-volume graviton modes, and construct a multimode squeezing operator. A rotating-wave approximation drops rapidly oscillating mixed creation–annihilation terms for sufficiently long interaction times.

Static suspended-quark solutions follow from a charged particle plus string worldsheet action in a probe RN background. For many strings, the authors solve spherical Einstein equations using a smeared radial-string stress tensor and match the exterior to RN.

A flat-space capacitor supplies an energy-comparison model and a Schwinger tunnelling estimate S ∼ mq²/(eE − ΛN²). The authors compare intact long strings with configurations containing an additional quark–antiquark pair.

Compare constant and temperature-dependent dissipation across both potentials. For VII, the numerical discussion stops expansion at H=0 and switches the Hubble sign for contraction. Analytic growth-rate comparisons and an effective radiation equation of state supplement the contracting numerical examples.

Numerically integrate the background system in N=ln a. Thawing initial conditions use Ωφ=10^−6 and φ′≈0 during matter domination, with illustrative ΩDR=10^−8. Present day is the earliest Ωm=0.3 crossing; shooting adjusts the initial field to obtain H(0)=H0.

Use Bianchi identities, integration by parts, leading equations of motion and the four-dimensional Gauss–Bonnet identity to organize redundancies. For probe backreaction, perturb both Maxwell and Einstein equations and exploit the O5 metric field redefinition.

Review the iterative solution of the modified Maxwell and Einstein equations around RN at first order in Wilson coefficients, then transform the corrected metric to isotropic coordinates before boosting.
Take a regulated distributional ultra-relativistic limit with m0 = γm and q0² = γq² held fixed, yielding a shock localized at u = 0.

The authors describe absorbing UV divergences into renormalized parameters and counterterms. A Poisson-resummed representation expresses the finite-radius contribution through modified Bessel functions, with exponential suppression for massive states.

Circle dimensional reduction and scalar KK expansion are followed by a Coleman–Weinberg tower contribution with field-dependent masses Meff,n² = Mi²(Φ) + n²/R². Only scalar fluctuations enter the implemented loop potential.

Vary the measure, metric and auxiliary gauge fields, then integrate the gauge equation. Independent string quantization treats each Ti as boundary data; the text also describes functional integration of the auxiliary gauge field.

Use a special conformal transformation to construct two conformally related flat metrics, infer tensions from their conformal ratio, and calculate the induced bubble geometry using comoving proper time.

Compute W, K and the geometric-to-Kähler-coordinate map to specified, possibly different orders; insert them into the scalar potential and compute, bound or estimate the remaining error. Numerical searches and stability analyses are introduced as computational strategies, without supplied detailed implementations or results.

Harmonic-form dimensional reduction and cohomology identify light fields; Weil–Petersson geometry determines moduli kinetic terms. Intersection numbers and mirror large-complex-structure prepotentials, including genus-zero Gopakumar–Vafa invariants, encode geometric and instanton data.

The primal bootstrap analytically removes gamma-function ansatz dependencies using Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z) and s+t+u=0, then uses SDPB to maximize selected couplings subject to residue positivity in both helicity channels.

Fixed-t dispersion relations and crossing require the direct-channel pole sum to generate a crossed-channel pole. Large-spin Wigner asymptotics constrain coupling decay; weighted integrals of discontinuities then diagnose failure of polynomial boundedness.

An alternative proof uses the spinning Froissart-Gribov projection after subtracting the universal infrared contribution of the graviton pole. Neglecting the contour at infinity requires partial-wave spin J>α(s).

Use harmonic-form expansions and special geometry to match zero-mode obstructions to derivatives of the leading four-dimensional potential. Estimate stability through Hessian projections and induced vacuum shifts. The calculation targets the potential; compensator-dependent kinetic terms are not derived.

Expand ten-dimensional fields in 1/c, with c ∼ V^(2/3). Subtract Laplacian zero-mode sources, retain the corresponding light fields off shell, solve the orthogonal triangular Poisson system iteratively, and insert the resulting profiles into the action.
Holographic renormalization supplies stress tensors and finite Euclidean on-shell actions. Differences between states at the same H eliminate scheme ambiguities and are used to compare branches.
Continue the bulk solution inside the event horizon to locate the apparent horizon, then assign QFT entropy from its area in the preferred ingoing-null slicing.

Numerical horizon shooting in Eddington–Finkelstein coordinates: fix the event horizon at uh=1, scan the horizon scalar φh, integrate outward, and fit boundary expansions to extract M, ξ and φ2. These determine the stress tensor and the ratio M/H.

Use mirror-symmetry periods and B-brane central charges to obtain monodromies from Fourier–Mukai transforms. Compare the induced tensorial transformation of three-point couplings with modular transformations of their explicit quasi-Jacobi expressions.

Package fibral genus-zero invariants into elliptic trilogarithm sums ΦR. Triple derivatives produce deformed Eisenstein series Jn; weight sums are converted to representation traces using Weyl characters.

Reduce the BCOV holomorphic anomaly equation for four-point couplings in a large-base limit, take the holomorphic limit, and identify the antiholomorphic derivative with the E2 anomaly operator. Extract base-degree-zero and, where required, q⁰ coefficients.

Duality transformations generate secondary BPS branes from primary fundamental strings, D-branes, NS5-branes or KK monopoles. Invariance of the BPS tension formula maps a primary light-tension region A to a secondary region g(A).

The operational gauge test compares transport along two timelike paths with common endpoints. Their transported states must differ by g while integrated environmental disturbances and proper acceleration can be made arbitrarily small. This is presented as a sufficient test.

For loops, use an imported curvature-squared effective action with local R²/Rµν² and nonlocal curvature-logarithm terms. Its linearized representation introduces massive spin-zero and spin-two gravitational fields; their large-mass elimination gives contact interactions.

Linearize gµν=ηµν+hµν/MP, impose de Donder gauge on the Fierz–Pauli action, invert the graviton kinetic operator, and integrate the linear stress-tensor coupling. Expand the resulting quadratic stress-tensor functional into scalar, fermion, vector and mixed sectors.

One-loop effective potentials are obtained from zero-external-momentum 1PI diagrams or background-field functional determinants. Thermal corrections use imaginary-time field theory and high-temperature expansions.

Relic calculations combine phase-transition-dependent monopole production, monopole–antimonopole annihilation and vector-boson freeze-out, including annihilation into dark particles and Standard Model Higgs bosons.

Direct/transverse-channel torus, Klein-bottle, annulus and Möbius amplitudes; NSNS/RR source projectors; Jacobi character identities and oscillator-level counting. Brane stability is analyzed using the one-loop position-modulus Hessian.

Poisson resummation, modular unfolding and Bessel-function asymptotics extract the bulk Casimir potential. N=1 F-term supergravity, a matched Kähler correction, non-perturbative superpotentials and a large-volume expansion organize the stabilization proposal.

The symmetry search varies polynomial transformations δx=K·v^(k−1)·λ^(l−1), integrates by parts and separates independent velocity/spatial-derivative structures. This is an ansatz-based classification, rather than a classification of arbitrary transformations.

Degenerate-metric Killing tensors are defined as mixed tensors of rank (1,k−1), whose upper index lowered with g gives a totally symmetric tensor. Their defining equation uses first-kind Christoffel symbols, avoiding an inverse metric or an assumed Levi-Civita connection.
Noether currents supply invariants of brane trajectories interpreted as generalized geodesics. Integrated charges are conserved for Σ=Σ̃×R when the spatial slice Σ̃ is compact and boundaryless.

SMEFT expansions through dimension-6 and dimension-8 operators; chiral/nuclear EFT and lattice-QCD matching; cosmological EFT around FRW; EFT of inflation using the Goldstone mode of broken time translations. These organize observable-to-parameter mappings rather than identify a unique UV theory.

Explicit likelihood L(d|θ,ν), nuisance marginalization/profiling, Gaussian χ² with correlated covariance, and Fisher forecasting. Forecasts require qualification when likelihoods are non-Gaussian, model systematics dominate, or only combined probes break degeneracies. Preserved likelihoods and covariance products enable subsequent global inference.

Forward-limit dispersion relations provide positivity inequalities for EFT fits. Nonperturbative lattice and nuclear many-body calculations supply hadronic vacuum polarization, light-by-light contributions, currents and matrix elements, with uncertainty propagation through to detector observables.

Derive Smarr identities by integrating closed generalized Komar forms between infinity and a bifurcation surface; harmonic decompositions of horizon potentials supply restricted generalized zeroth laws.

Construct Noether and Noether–Wald forms using differential forms, compensating gauge transformations and electric/magnetic momentum maps; obtain generalized Komar forms by subtracting an alternative primitive of the on-shell Noether–Wald derivative.
Use covariant phase-space variations for first laws, retaining the commutator contribution caused by field-dependent compensating gauge parameters.
A Weyl transformation relates string-frame and Einstein-frame lengths to express the string cutoff entering cosmological bounds.
Raychaudhuri's equation, the comoving expansion scalar θ = 3H, and the FRW Kretschmann invariant provide diagnostics for the singularity discussion.
The author takes infinitesimal time intervals in Conjecture 2 and combines the resulting inequality with scalar Friedmann equations and an H(φ) formulation.

Wetterich FRG with modified local potential approximation LPA′: running wave-function factors enter the regulator, producing anomalous dimensions on both sides of the flow equations. Two functional derivatives and kinetic-term projections determine their algebraic self-consistency equations.

The calculation imports matter-only axion–photon and pure Einstein–Hilbert inputs, adds minimal gravitational dressing, and studies the determinant of the resulting anomalous-dimension matrix. A block-determinant argument estimates the effect of restoring small sector mixing.

Back-to-back resummation factorizes hard scattering from eikonal graviton phases, Fourier transforms the transverse recoil constraint and evaluates the soft factor by Gaussian averaging. String corrections use supersymmetric KLT relations and a low-energy expansion of world-sheet integrals.

NLO combines the one-loop four-point virtual contribution with the integrated tree-level five-point real contribution. The authors use dimensional regularization d=4−2ε with ε<0 for infrared divergences, phase-space reduction and van Neerven integrals.

Endpoint terms are distributions on the detector sphere. At z=1, the azimuth β degenerates, so smooth test functions become β-independent; extracting the contact term requires averaging its residue over β, together with a spherical plus prescription.

Local f is Taylor-expanded about an AdS extremum with f^(0)=√(−V_0/3) and f^(1)=0. The authors describe 2^4=16 Hessian branches, followed by linear equations for higher coefficients. Low-Hessian branches generate candidate interpolating walls; high-Hessian branches are used for bounding functions.

Reducing the action to one radial dimension and imposing the zero-Hamiltonian constraint yields a separable HJ ansatz F=2e^(3A)f. The fake superpotential obeys V=−3f²+2K^ij∂_if∂_jf, generating first-order wall equations.
Obtain F=I_E/β, S=−∂F/∂T and M=F+TS. Use the unperturbed horizon radius as an intermediate variable and differentiate through its temperature relation.

Regularize AdS actions by background subtraction with matched Euclidean periods. Use Wald entropy to convert results from unperturbed radius r̄_h to perturbed radius r_h without constructing the perturbed metric.

Evaluate I₀+γI_ehd on the unperturbed saddle with matched boundary data: stationarity suppresses the I₀ metric-variation term to O(γ²), while the explicit γ similarly suppresses corrections inside I_ehd.

KK expansion gives mass matrices diagonalized through MiMi† in vacuum. Matter adds an active-sector weak potential; truncation at KK label N produces a 3(N+1)-dimensional matrix H whose eigenvalues and eigenvectors determine coherent flavor-transition amplitudes.
Gaussian elimination reduces the characteristic problem to a 3×3 matrix T(x), with x=R²m². Infinite KK sums are resummed into cot expressions and their coth continuation below x=c̄i².

Modified GLoBES generates spectra. A binned Poisson χ² uses Gaussian systematic pulls and parameter priors. Two fits keep standard oscillation parameters fixed or marginalize θ13 and Δm²32 together with systematic nuisance parameters.

Oscillation probabilities are computed numerically for normal ordering using a 12-layer PREM Earth-density profile. Energy–zenith oscillograms identify where the additional potential changes muon-neutrino survival.

A frequentist modified χ² sums squared event residuals divided by Nexp+(σsim)², plus Gaussian nuisance pulls. Profiles compare a fixed LRI potential with its freely fitted value. Twenty nuisance parameters, including two atmospheric oscillation parameters, are minimized simultaneously.

A forward-folding analysis reweights IceCube Monte Carlo through PISA for atmospheric flux, interaction cross sections, oscillations and detector response. Reconstructed energy, direction and BDT particle-identification scores define the event distributions.

Heavy-quark matching and running estimate κ at the QCD scale. Mixing with the vector-like quark is used to estimate weak-current shifts, while the dimension-five operator determines a three-body Higgs decay width.

An anomalous PQ rotation removes θ through the Fujikawa measure. Chiral effective theory uses the spurion M=diag(κφ,md,ms) and analyzes the neutral pseudoscalar sector containing a, π3, η8 and η1, including a phenomenological anomaly mass for η1.

Photon form factors and FCNC operators are estimated with quark loops. An octet-baryon mass fit estimates scalar/nucleon couplings, giving a proton coupling 1.47κφp̄LpR plus its conjugate and no neutron coupling within that treatment.
Solve the 5D Einstein equations using ds²=n²dt²−a²δ_ij dx^i dx^j−dy², then impose brane junction conditions and compactification boundary conditions to obtain the brane Friedmann equations.

Compute Hubble/potential slow-roll hierarchies and scalar/tensor spectra, including a geometry-dependent effective Planck mass for tensors; perform χ² fits to n_s−1, running α, scalar amplitude Δ_s² and tensor ratio r using two observational compilations.
Adopt the horizon first law with S_A=A/(4G) and T=1/(2πR) to obtain a modified Friedmann constraint; combine it with ρ̇+DH(ρ+p)=0 to formulate background evolution and scalar-field damping.

Conjecture a fractal horizon-crossing relation, transform the spatial Laplacian to define k_eff, and use a modified Mukhanov–Sasaki equation with a proposed Bunch–Davies initialization to estimate the scalar spectrum and tilt.

Derive slow-roll parameters and e-fold integrals; illustrate linear/cubic evolution numerically. For Starobinsky inflation, use a conformal transformation and field redefinition to work with an Einstein-frame potential.

Solve scalar modes exactly in de Sitter space using Hankel functions with order ς²=9/4−m²/H²−12ξ. Select the Bunch–Davies state by its short-wavelength positive-frequency limit. Evaluate EMT integrals through dimensional regularization and special-function identities.

Use off-shell adiabatic subtraction: ⟨Tμν⟩ren(M)=⟨Tμν⟩(m)−⟨Tμν⟩(0–4)(M). The subtraction includes adiabatic orders 0, 2 and 4; Δ²=m²−M² counts as order 2. Generic FLRW on-shell quantities require a truncated WKB expansion instead of exact modes.

Insert the derived vacuum density into the cosmological equations for vacuum–radiation exchange. The full digamma-dependent density requires numerical evolution; freezing its slowly varying H² coefficient permits an approximate analytic solution.

Compare Ricci, Kretschmann and squared Weyl invariants using background/local/interaction decompositions. Multithroat interactions and knot deformations are treated as localized perturbations at leading nontrivial order; Appendix C supplies illustrative numerical energy-condition diagnostics.

Describe marked throat histories by braid movies with generators σᵢ±¹. The signed generator sum supplies chirality bookkeeping, while ∫W C* C is only schematically related to weighted generator events, without an equality or quantization claim.

Illustrate projection-induced nonlocality by eliminating A₀ in electrodynamics and integrating out a fakeon field from a local parent Lagrangian. Nonlocal dressed electron observables provide a further example, with the inverse-operator prescription affecting Lorentz invariance and physical degrees of freedom.
Compare retarded and advanced electromagnetic dipole solutions generated by the same conserved current. Selection between them is assigned to boundary conditions rather than to the current alone.

Invert higher-derivative operators with prescribed Green functions: Dirac's acceleration uses an exponentially damped future-force integral, while the fakeon acceleration uses a time-symmetric sine kernel integrated over all times.

Rewrite the free thermal partition function as a unitary-matrix integral, then integrate Fourier modes of continuous eigenvalue densities at large N. Locate the Hagedorn singularity through loss of positive definiteness of the Gaussian Hessian.

Express the quadratic interaction through the quiver adjacency matrix A. Collatz–Wielandt and Rayleigh-quotient bounds, combined with conformal balancing, constrain its largest eigenvalue and hence the Hagedorn temperature.

Use the tree-level localized S⁴ partition function to obtain the asymptotic Zamolodchikov metric, introduce orthonormal logarithmic gauge-coupling coordinates, and construct scalar charge-to-mass vectors and their convex hull.

Dimensionally reduce the Lovelock action, integrate derivative terms, and transform from Jordan to Einstein frame. Test the potential curvature, graviton coefficient K and scalar kinetic coefficient N at a tuned Minkowski extremum.

Compute curvature invariants through cubic order from symmetric-space structure constants, isotropy representations, Casimirs and normalization-independent Dynkin-index ratios. The appendix describes tensor-product trace reduction and birdtrack calculations.

Factor the cubic-model potential around a double Minkowski root and analyze zeros of a quadratic polynomial proportional to K. Their position relative to the negative-potential region determines the proposed kinetic-barrier window.
Euclidean path-integral state preparation and gluing compute TFT overlaps; normalized insertions are compared between boundary factorization and bulk fillings with different cycle topology.

Lorentzian analysis uses thermofield-double purification, cutting and gluing across the horizon, linking-matrix changes of basis, and entanglement-wedge reconstruction. Identifying the sphere-cut charge and point-defect basis expansions requires the stated condition that the linking matrix S be unitary.
Background treatment uses dissipative inflaton evolution, radiation production, and the Friedmann equation. Under the stated slow-roll approximation these give 3H(1+Q)ϕ̇=−V′ and ρr=3Qϕ̇²/4.

The authors report numerical background and perturbation calculations with WI2easy in Mathematica, using e-fold number N as time and four benchmarks BP1–BP4. They calibrate the potential amplitude to the quoted Planck scalar amplitude and report convergence and agreement with another solver; these checks are author reports.

Scalar perturbations include a thermal occupation contribution and a growth factor G(Q). The paper states G(Q)=1+4.981Q^1.946+0.127Q^4.33 and defines ns through the logarithmic derivative of the scalar spectrum. The extracted spectrum normalization is not sufficiently clear for reconstruction.

Canonically normalize Kähler moduli and use autonomous-system fixed points for exponential potentials. Compute spectral slopes by integrating redshifted loop emission and comparing formation-time, half-energy-time and late-time contributions.

Combine a conjectured species-scale gradient bound with the Friedmann equation and Cauchy–Schwarz inequality; integrate for monotonically decreasing species scale. The authors then infer tension bounds, but their μ(t₀)-normalized finite-epoch transfer requires an additional evolution relation beyond pointwise μ≥Λ_s².

Apply decay and fission or quiver subtraction, then compare resulting Higgsing directions with F-theory curve configurations and their discrete flavor permutations. Mitosis supplies an additional transition-multiplicity operation.

Use monopole-formula Hilbert series and plethystic logarithms to test global symmetries and chiral rings. Examples include 1+82t²+… for expected O(5)×O(9)² and a reproduced 1+156t²+… series for E₆×E₆.

Employ Hanany–Witten brane transitions and 3d mirror constructions. A doubled Type IIB setup is described by chain polymerization along diagonal SU(n)⊆SU(k)×SU(k), with n≤2N≤k, supported by sample Hilbert-series comparisons.

On-shell N=4 superspace packages component amplitudes and their Ward identities. A basis change produces a six-term NMHV identity relating Z1=A6[z1 z2 z3 z̄3 z̄1 z̄2] to its cyclic momentum relabelings. The identity is imposed order by order in the EFT expansion.

Dispersion relations express Wilson coefficients as positive spectral moments with Legendre-polynomial weights. SDPB implements crossing and additional null constraints; eliminating g and fixing a2,0/a0,0 permits many nonlinear relations to be imposed as linear constraints on each numerical slice.

Bottom-up amplitude construction matches residues to lower-point products and parametrizes remaining local polynomials. Z1 has poles only in channels 34, 234, and 345. BCFW shifts preserve momentum conservation on poles; the authors use rational kinematics and finite-field methods for large linear systems.

Solve the right-handed-neutrino anomaly conditions ΣQ_i=−3 and ΣQ_i³=−3 over real charges, examining a branch where one charge approaches −3 while the other two become large and approximately opposite.

Calculate neutrino two-body decay and light-mediator scattering, then apply imported lifetime and scattering limits and compare with fifth-force exclusions. The scattering bound is recast from an existing universal tensor-model analysis rather than obtained from a new detector-data fit.

Flux backtracking solves BPS flow equations using fluxes that do not scale with N. A harmonic superposition ansatz then introduces the D4 stacks. The author reports checking the ten-dimensional Einstein and dilaton equations and imposing D4 flux quantization.

Decoupling diagnostics comprise Einstein-frame gravitational redshift and radial propagation of transverse traceless gravitons. A field redefinition produces a Schrödinger-like equation; minimally coupled scalar s-waves yield the same effective potential.

Normalized metric one-point functions are represented by displaced-vacuum path integrals. A Fourier-space three-scalar surrogate is evaluated using Gaussian integrals, momentum combinatorics and tree, first-order and Nth-order expansions; volume-suppressed contributions are discarded.

Dimensional reduction/uplift, T-duality and type-I/heterotic S-duality track metrics, fluxes and couplings. The unbroken E8×E8 construction additionally prescribes blow-ups before reduction along the remaining orbifold interval.

Uses previously constructed two-dimensional Horndeski master equations. Variations with respect to q_ab and r define a generalized spherical Einstein tensor that is symmetric, second order and covariantly conserved.
Reconstruction uses α=∂_rΩ and β=∂_χΩ, with Ω constant on shell. One action representation is H_2=α, H_3=−2β and H_4=−∫dr β; integrations by parts make this representation nonunique.

Encode infinite coupling expansions through finite differential systems or recursion relations. Examples use Pfaffian chains, Log-Noetherian functions, exact zero-dimensional integration, and Seiberg–Witten differential relations. Exact RG equations are explored as a possible extension.

Use an FD-filtration of definable sets: unions/intersections maximize format and add degrees; projections and complements preserve the assigned bounds. Sharp o-minimality bounds one-dimensional connected components by a format-dependent polynomial in degree.
Additional methods are pion-loop hadronic matching, VY anomaly matching with small-mass/1/N expansions, and the matrix determinant lemma for the axion–meson mass matrix.

CCWZ nonlinear realization and an O(p²) chiral Lagrangian organize meson and baryon interactions. Introducing Q without a kinetic term and eliminating it algebraically produces the anomaly potential; stationarity gives the Dashen equations.

Substitute the kinetic-to-potential ratio into the background equations, differentiate the ansatz, and obtain a differential constraint relating β(φ) and V(φ). Solve it for a rational β and examine large- and small-field limits.

Compare potential slow-roll parameters and their e-fold integral with direct background indices ε1, ε2 and a full-ansatz e-fold expression. Evaluate ns and r at the specified initial horizon crossing and compare with quoted observational regions.

Uses the Wetterich functional RG equation and background-field method, with linear metric/vector splits, gravitational gauge fixing and Faddeev–Popov ghosts. Beta functions are extracted by matching background operators.

Adds couplings successively and tracks fixed-point coordinates together with stability-matrix eigenvalues. Critical exponents help distinguish nearby branches whose coordinates alone give ambiguous identifications.

The regularized Hessian is inverted using block-matrix inversion and two Parker–Fulling expansions. Open derivatives and Laplacian functions are reordered with commutators before heat-kernel evaluation; the symbolic calculation uses xAct.

For ℓ≥2, diagonalize the leading coupled gravito-electromagnetic equations and obtain corrections through Green-function convolution. Define pure external gravitational or magnetic sources by their leading asymptotic growth, then compare response tails with STF worldline operators.

Expand the quadratic perturbation action to first order in αi, introduce auxiliary master variables, and eliminate algebraic constraints. Solve sourced equations using the zeroth-order differential operator. Horizon regularity, removal of residual gauge modes and, for the odd dipole, removal of the small-rotation mode select the response.
